📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

He needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

When Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

In a recent development, it proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

Industry observers note that “It was a really good fight,” Alisson stated, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”.

Any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

Industry observers note that “He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola stated. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”.

Don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

Isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

Cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards. Liverpool never looked back.

Industry observers note that alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4.

According to recent reports, “A striker’s job is like this,” Iraola remarked, who badgered Isak persistently to press Bournemouth’s defence. “He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control. He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”.

Industry observers note that one, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

“Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose mentioned. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola said: “I’m obviously happy with the result because I know this is a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. And we could see it, especially in the beginning of the game. In the first 20 minutes we weren’t at the level [required] and it cost us. We finished the first half better and in the second half we played better, but that beginning of the game has surprised us, not surprised us [because] we knew where we were coming but it [was] difficult for us.”.

Jeremy Jacquet has made the kind of quietly authoritative start to his Liverpool career that indicated why there was such excitement in February within the club when they completed his deal. So much focus on so many players but Jacquet has never been anything other 7.5/8 out of 10.

"Let's go! One of many!" Virgil van Dijk giving Jérémy Jacquet his POTM award after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/6xWvjmrF8Y.

In a recent development, "That's a big moment to me to play with Virgil!" 🫡Jérémy Jacquet after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth! pic.twitter.com/UsTimGME39.

Sources indicate that cody Gakpo has been Liverpool’s stand-out forward this term and he was at the heart of Isak’s goal this afternoon. Speaking about the job the Dutchman is doing to fill the void left by Mohamed Salah on the right flank, Ashley Young noted on Sky Sports: “Players have to step up when you lose big players and you get the opportunities. I think Cody Gakpo is doing that. He’s a bit fortunate [in the build-up to Liverpool’s goal] but you create your own luck. He gets the ball down the line, that’s what you want to do and he puts the ball in the box. That’s what Isak’s waiting for.”.

Recent findings suggest that andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

Recent findings suggest that his first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

According to recent reports, everything Iraola has noted and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that there is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has said that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he noted: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

Recent findings suggest that “We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”.

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

It has been revealed that adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He said: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”.

Truffert topped the charts for most overlapping runs by any player in Europe’s top five leagues last season and laid on five assists.

Speaking before his return to the South Coast, Iraola noted: “I know where we are going [the Vitality], and I know the stats they have there [unbeaten in 12 matches], not only in their stadium, overall, I think if you see the games they’ve lost in a long while, you realise how difficult it is to beat Bournemouth.

“But, I suppose I also have the advantage that I know them very well, they also have the advantage that they know me very well, so you never know who has more advantage in that sense.

It has been revealed that he added: “On a personal side, I’m very much looking forward to meet them [his former players], to hug them. It’s players that I love, staff that I’ve been working with who I appreciate so much, and I was pushing for them [against Real Sociedad] when they were playing their first European game. I wish them all the best, but there is another part, which is the most important one right now that we need to go there and win.”.

Just the one alternation to the side Rose fielded last weekend as Christie comes in for Kluivert.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his big move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to upcoming heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, mentioned: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”.

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

Liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

The Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

UEFA Nations League Preview | Germany eye UEFA Nations League quarter-final berth

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that under Jürgen Klopp, the German national team hopes to reach the quarter-finals of the UEFA Nations League, set to take place in March 2027.
  • Netherlands lead the group with 11 points, while Greece and Germany are level with eight points heading into the final group stage game.
  • Germany need a win to secure qualification.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that under Jürgen Klopp, the German national team hopes to reach the quarter-finals of the UEFA Nations League, set to take place in March 2027. Standing in their way is a reinvigorated Netherlands side that defeated Greece 7-0 on the final matchday.

Netherlands lead the group with 11 points, while Greece and Germany are level with eight points heading into the final group stage game.

Germany need a win to secure qualification. In the case of a draw, the team will be hoping that Greece doesn’t get a better result against bottom side Serbia.

During the last international break, Germany started their group with a draw against the Netherlands and a 1-0 loss against Greece. The performances were far from perfect and gave Klopp a lot to think about.

Those games were followed by a win against Serbia and a 0-0 draw against Greece away from home. The games served as a preview of which areas the team needs to focus on.

During this international break, Klopp called up 24 players in contrast to the expanded 44-man squad in October. This reveals that the coach has identified which players can make an impact at the national team.

The 3-1 away win against Serbia was encouraging and saw two of the national team’s key players, Florian Wirtz and Brajan Gruda, get on the scoresheet.

“The team put in a truly outstanding performance. I think we need to get used to the fact that we’re really good and that we can play really good football. We could have scored more goals today. But I told the players earlier that, at this moment, I really don’t care about that. There were so many outstanding moments today,” Klopp noted after the game.

The team seems to understand the coach’s expectations well this time around and can face the challenge that will be posed by the Netherlands in better form than was the case a month ago.

In a recent development, klopp stated that the game is like a final. “We wanted to set up a final against the Netherlands in Berlin, and now we have it. We now have the chance to secure qualification for the next round in our own hands. We want to show everyone that German football is in good hands. We have good players, we’re working hard, and we want to show in these matches that we’ve learned, that we’ve come together and that we’ve developed as a team. And that was definitely evident today. The atmosphere in the camp is good, but that means nothing if nobody can see it on the pitch. Our first job is to show the world that we can play football.”.

75,000 spectators are expected to attend the game at the Olympic Stadium in Berlin as Germany wear their Adidas farewell kit for the last time before switching to Nike in 2027. In a game that is labelled a ‘mini-final’ for Klopp, all eyes will be on the team as they not only fight for qualification to the quarter-finals but also to preserve their status in the UEFA Nations League A group.

It has been revealed that kat Kerkhofs, moglie dell’ex azzurro Dries Mertens, ha rilasciato un’intervista a DH Les Sports: “Perché abbiamo scelto di vivere alle Isole Baleari? L’idea iniziale era di tornare a vivere a Napoli dopo la fine della carriera di Dries. Ma lì è troppo famoso, e la sua presenza invade la nostra vita quotidiana. I viaggi e la vita in camper? Dries ne aveva bisogno dopo la sua carriera. Era stufo degli allenamenti, dei ritiri e degli hotel in città dove non vedeva altro che lo stadio e l’aeroporto. Voleva liberarsi dalle routine imposte e riconquistare la sua libertà”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 16:54 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 20:17 EST, 12 November 2026.
  • Only giants have trodden the path that Harry Kane walked at Wembley on Thursday when he strode out on to the pitch on a bitterly cold winter night, his four young children by his side, and beheld the array of trophies, honours, adulation and respect that awaited him.
  • It is just 16 days since Kane held his hands to his face, climbed up to the stage at the London Palladium and mentioned 'wow' when Ronaldo 'Il Fenomeno' presented him with the Ballon d'Or trophy that anointed him the best player in the world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 16:54 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 20:17 EST, 12 November 2026.

Only giants have trodden the path that Harry Kane walked at Wembley on Thursday when he strode out on to the pitch on a bitterly cold winter night, his four young children by his side, and beheld the array of trophies, honours, adulation and respect that awaited him.

It is just 16 days since Kane held his hands to his face, climbed up to the stage at the London Palladium and mentioned 'wow' when Ronaldo 'Il Fenomeno' presented him with the Ballon d'Or trophy that anointed him the best player in the world.

Now, it sat before him on a plinth and Kane broke away from the England line-up and walked forward to hoist it aloft. He demonstrated it to all the corners of the stadium and for a moment, it was framed against the giant tifo bearing his image and the words 'England's Finest' that towered over one end of the ground.

But the Ballon d’Or is old news in the flood of honours that is coming Kane’s way in this golden summer of a great career. Kane had become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or for a quarter of a century and on Thursday night he was to break the 37-year-old record held by Peter Shilton for the most England caps. He scored the winner, too. Of course, he did.

The occasion of England-Croatia in the Nations League was Kane's 126th appearance in an England shirt and Shilton stepped forward to hand him a small case containing a crest to mark the achievement. Finally, the Prince of Wales showed his appreciation to the England captain by presenting him with a commemorative shirt with 'Kane 126' emblazoned on it.

It was a night to feel the weight of football's history and the ghosts of greatness that people England's heritage. Kane belongs in the tech giant he now keeps. He belongs in the pantheon of the game because he is one of the deadliest strikers in history. He belongs in the pantheon because of the humility he has shown and the dedication he devotes to improvement.

Harry Kane celebrated his record-breaking England appearance with a finely struck penalty.

Before kick-off, Kane's history-making was celebrated with a commemorative shirt by the Prince of Wales.

England (4-2-3-1): Pickford 6; Alexander-Arnold 6 (White 78, 6), Quansah 4, Burn 6, Hall 7; Rice 5 (Garner 78, 5), Anderson 6; Rogers 8, Bellingham 6, Gordon 5 (Ngumoha 78, 5); Kane 7.

Goals: Rogers 24', Kane 64' (pen).

Croatia (4-2-3-1): Livakovic 5; Smolcic 6 (Marco Pasalic 76 5), Stanisic 6, Vuskovic 6, Gvardiol 5; Misic 5 (Modric 76, 6), Kovacic 6; Sucic 7 (Mario Pasalic 70, 5), Baturina 6, Vlasic 5; Matanovic 5 (Budimir 70, 5).

He belongs with Billy Wright, the first England player to 100 caps, and the man who set the England appearance record at 105 when he played for his country for the last time in 1959. He belongs with Bobby Charlton, who made it to 106 before the heartbreak of the 1970 World Cup quarter-final defeat to West Germany brought his international career to an end.

In a recent development, kane belongs with Bobby Moore, Charlton's rival as the greatest England player of all time, who reached the newly introduced mark of 108 caps in November 1973. That was one of the great numbers in English sport until Peter Shilton finally surpassed it. He reached 125 caps by the time he played his last game for England in the third-place play-off at the 1990 World Cup.

Industry observers note that it is quite some lineage. And now it is Kane who holds the prize. And if this was hardly a momentous match, it was a momentous occasion. If you are tired of glorying in a player like Kane, a relentless striker, a wonderful passer, the sweetest striker of the ball you will ever see, a player of vision, a man who exudes the beauty of simplicity and the wonder of modesty, then you are tired of football.

Industry observers note that the honours are rushing at him in a giddy, babbling flood. It may be that he reaches close to 200 caps before he retires and even if it already seems likely that that record will be broken by Jude Bellingham, who has 61 caps at the age of 23, Kane's England goals tally, which stands at 92 after another goal against Croatia, will not be under threat for a generation or longer.

The gap, of course, is a tournament victory. That is what still separates Moore and Charlton from him. Kane is a dream of a player but he has not won the World Cup or the European Championship. What remains is the hope that he will put that right in the years that he has left in the game.

Winning the Nations League would not be quite the same but it would be a start and this victory over Croatia took England a small step closer to that goal. A convincing win over Spain in Madrid on Sunday would take them closer to their aim of finishing top of this group and getting a favourable draw in the quarter-finals in the spring.

According to recent reports, kane made his England debut in March 2015 when he was 21 and England's future looks brighter now than it did when he broke through. More than an hour before the game, the men who will follow Kane and perhaps even chase his caps record, chatted animatedly on the pitch. Bellingham, Morgan Rogers, Anthony Gordon and Morgan Gibbs-White are the new breed.

Morgan Rogers opened the scoring inside the opening half-an-hour and celebrated with his trademark cold celebration.

England had found themselves pegged back by Croatia after slopping defending drew the visitors level.

Referee Morten Krogh was summoned to the monitor to review the penalty shout on Thursday.

Kane returned to Wembley triumphant for the first time since his historic Ballon d'Or win.

After the Kane festivities, the first half was an anti-climax. Twenty-four minutes of relative drudgery ensued before Kane exhibited the breadth of his talent once again to help put England ahead. He got the ball 30 yards out, looked up and drifted a beautiful diagonal pass out to the right and into the path of Bellingham. Bellingham volleyed it across goal and Rogers forced it over the line.

The second half began slowly, too, but 15 minutes into it, Croatia equalised. England failed to clear a corner, Jarell Quansah tried to head the ball back to Jordan Pickford and, as Kane watched on, Petar Sucic stole in and hooked the ball past the England goalkeeper into the roof of the net.

Industry observers note that quansah made some kind of amends three minutes later when he was dragged down in the box and Danish referee Morten Krogh awarded a penalty. It was Kane-time again. Kane took the kick and lifted it gently and with a touch of curl down the centre of the goal. Dominic Livakovic dived to his left and the ball sailed softly over his trailing leg and into the net.

Recent findings suggest that croatia had chances to draw level but could not take them. England made changes and young Rio Ngumoha, a winger of rare talent, another with a rich future ahead of him, another who will help to fill the void when the day comes for Kane to bid farewell to England, came on as a late substitute for Gordon.

And so Kane's night of history began to draw to a close. In a 2-1 victory, he had made one and scored one. He remains as central to England's hopes of ending more than 60 years without a trophy as he ever has been. In a career that has festooned him with garlands and left no one in doubt of his greatness, it is the only gap that remains.

Harry Kane has set his sights firmly on rapidly reaching a century of international goals after becoming England’s most-capped player of all time.

The England skipper marked his 126th appearance for the Three Lions with the winner against Croatia in the Nations League – his first goal since picking up the Ballon d’Or last month.

Kane was afforded an emotional presentation pre-match at Wembley to mark both achievements and is already thinking of creating more history after moving within eight goals of a ton.

‘It’s achievable,’ Kane remarked. ‘I’m getting closer. Breaking the appearance record is a massive thing in the history of our game, seeing the tifo at the stadium and having my kids with me was beyond dreams.

‘It’s important to recognise our great players. It’s maybe something we haven’t done so well over the years with some of our other greats.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It's been a crazy few weeks. I don’t know if I’ve fully taken it all in. The reception has been overwhelming.

‘Maybe during the winter break I’ll be on a beach reflecting on everything I’ve achieved, having a drink with my wife.’.

Croatia legend Luka Modric, 41, was part of the presentations ahead of kick off and Kane did not rule out attempting to prolong his career in a similar vein to the AC Milan midfielder.

Industry observers note that ‘He’s an inspiration for a lot of us,’ Kane added. ‘An incredible player and a great person, he’s looked after himself and still to be playing at this level is inspiring for me to push the limits. To see where your body and mentality takes you.

According to recent reports, ‘As long as I feel I can help, I’ll be here for as long as I can. If that’s until I’m 40, we’ll wait and see.’.

Now qualified for the quarter-finals, England need to beat Spain in Madrid on Sunday to top their group and Thomas Tuchel believes they can topple the world champions.

Sources indicate that ‘It’s a completely different scenario, completely different setup,’ Tuchel mentioned. ‘But I'm very positive that we will get what we want.’.

Germany host Group A2 leaders the Netherlands in their final UEFA Nations League group stage game with a win enough to take Jürgen Klopp’s charges through to the quarter-finals.

Speaking at Sunday’s press conference, Klopp kept his card close to his chest when asked about any potential changes. Nico Schlotterbeck, who didn’t feature in Germany’s 3-1 victory over Serbia, could start ahead of Malick Thiaw, but the national team head coach has somewhat of a dilemma in central defence. “Central defence is a position where I feel very comfortable,” explained Klopp.

“It’s a very crucial position. If everything else falls apart, the two centre-backs and the goalkeeper is the last line of defence. The guys who are here are top players, and Waldemar Anton, who is at home injured, is also a top player. There are also top players in the U21 squad.”.

According to Kicker, Schlotterbeck may be the only change, but Bild also have Bayern Munich’s Nathaniel Brown starting ahead of Maximilian Mittelstädt so, at most, Klopp may only make two changes for tonight’s clash against the Dutch at the Olympiastadion, where Kai Havertz is again expected to lead the attack.

Bayer Leverkusen playmaker Ibrahim Maza has sustained an ankle injury while on international duty, the Algerian Football Federation (FAF) has confirmed.

Industry observers note that the 20-year-old suffered an ankle strain during Saturday’s Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Togo and, following medical examinations, will not travel to Togo for the second-leg on Tuesday. The FAF did not provide further details on Maza’s absence.

This, of course, is a concern for Bayer Leverkusen ahead of Saturday’s Bundesliga game against Paderborn but, per Bild, Bayer hope that Maza will be available.

Under Carles Martínez, Maza (20) is shining. With three goals and three assists in nine Bundesliga games in 2026/27, the Berlin-born Algeria international is close to surpassing last season’s tally of three goals and five assists in 28 Bundesliga appearances.

A key player for die Werkself, Leverkusen managing director for sport Simon Rolfes confirmed that the club are in talks to extend Maza’s contract beyond 2030.

According to recent reports, holstein Kiel’s striker Adrián Kaprálik saved Slovakia’s unbeaten record in the 2026/27 UEFA Nations League with a 95th-minute equalizer against Kazakhstan. The 24-year-old scored his first goal for the senior national team as Slovakia win promotion to League B with 12 points.

After his debut appearance in the 2-2 draw with Faroe Islands, the Haarlem-born midfielder Ludovit Reis appeared off the bench as Vladimír Weiss’ side repeated that scoreline on Monday with the help of Kaprálik's strike. The Werder Bremen central midfielder decided to change his allegiance after "only a matter of one phone call", according to the head coach.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Reis’ club teammate Karl Hein and VfL Bochum's center-back Karol Mets helped Estonia to a 2-1 win over Lukas Petkov's Bulgaria on Monday. Estonia finished second in their group despite also finishing with 12 points. Mets is the captain of the team, while the Arsenal loanee won back his #1 spot after his solid performances for Bremen.

Despite Estonia's unbeaten campaign, they finished two points behind Ísak Jóhannesson's Iceland, who automatically won promotion to League B alongside Albania, Montenegro and Slovakia. The Köln midfielder started all six games for Iceland. Estonia, Belarus, Cyprus and Faroe Islands will enter playoff with bottom-placed teams from League B.

Sources indicate that A tre giorni dalla scadenza per le candidature alla presidenza della FIFA, la UEFA è ancora alla ricerca del candidato che sfiderà Gianni Infantino. Dopo aver preso in considerazione Sandor Csányi, presidente della Federazione calcistica ungherese, e poi Arsène Wenger, che alla fine si è ritirato, i vertici europei stanno ora valutando una nuova opzione.

Secondo le fonti del portale Footmercato, diversi funzionari della UEFA stanno attualmente promuovendo internamente l'ex Inter Luis Figo. L'ex nazionale portoghese, che aveva già tentato di candidarsi alla presidenza della FIFA nel 2015 prima di ritirarsi, non è tuttavia una scelta unanime all'interno della UEFA. Le discussioni proseguiranno quindi negli ultimi giorni prima della scadenza.

Sources indicate that la posta in gioco è alta per l'organo di governo del calcio europeo, che spera di presentare una candidatura congiunta contro Gianni Infantino, che cerca un quarto mandato dopo aver assunto la guida della FIFA nel 2016. L'elezione si terrà il 18 marzo 2027 a Rabat, in Marocco, durante il Congresso FIFA. Per essere ufficialmente selezionato, ogni candidato deve ottenere il sostegno di almeno cinque federazioni affiliate alla FIFA. I candidati hanno tempo fino al 18 novembre per presentare la propria candidatura. La UEFA ha quindi pochissimo tempo per raggiungere un accordo e stabilire se Luis Figo riuscirà a ottenere il consenso dei suoi vertici.

Jan Vertonghen, ex calciatore belga con un lungo passato all’Ajax, ha rilasciato alcune dichiarazioni ai microfoni di Voetbal Primeur a proposito del possibile trasferimento di De Bruyne al PSV al termine del match tra le leggende dell’Ajax e quelle del Barcellona. Di seguito le sue dichiarazioni: “A quanto pare, il suo desiderio è quello di vivere vicino a casa e Amsterdam è comunque un po’ più distante dal Limburgo belga. Credo quindi che la sua preferenza possa ricadere sul PSV. In ogni caso, sarebbe un grande acquisto per il campionato olandese. Alla fine, ciò che conta davvero per un calciatore è essere felice. Spesso, però, si capisce soltanto nella fase più avanzata della propria carriera cosa significhi davvero la felicità, dove si riesca a trovarla e da cosa dipenda: dai soldi, dai trofei, dalle strutture o dal benessere della propria famiglia. Anche per me, andando avanti con la carriera, la felicità della mia famiglia è diventata un fattore fondamentale. Potrebbe essere così anche per lui. Non ne ho parlato personalmente con Kevin, ma comprendo perfettamente il suo punto di vista”.

Jamal Musiala is set to return to Bayern Munich’s matchday squad for Friday’s Bundesliga clash against Cologne, according to Sport1.

The 23-year-old has been sidelined since suffering a torn muscle fibre during a warm-up prior to Germany’s UEFA Nations League game against the Netherlands on 24 September.

Musiala has featured just three times in the Bundesliga for Germany’s record champions this season, returning a goal and assist, while also scoring in his only UEFA Champions League game in 2026/27.

It goes without saying that this is providing that Musiala, who has been training for the last 10 days, doesn’t suffer any setbacks in training during the week.

Bayern could, however, be without Alphonso Davies. The 25-year-old sustained an injury while on international duty with Canada, lasting just six minutes of his nation’s 3-2 CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final win over Guatemala after picking up an injury on 13 November.

Speaking to Canada’s One Soccer, Davies noted: “At the beginning of the game everything seemed good. I fell down. They’re analysing the footage. I think my back twisted when I slipped. I tried to get up as quickly as possible to block the shot. As soon as I raised my leg and put it down to block the shot, I felt something […] Hopefully it’s not too bad.”.

L’ex allenatore riconosce le capacità del presidente e distingue il lavoro societario dal rapporto personale.

Delio Rossi riconosce a Claudio Lotito il merito di aver risanato il bilancio della Lazio, pur ricordando che, al suo arrivo, lo stipendio dell’allenatore contava più delle idee di gioco. Secondo quanto riportato da FanPage, In un’intervista a FanPage.it, l’ex tecnico ripercorre il rapporto con il presidente e racconta anche come conobbe Rino Gattuso a Salerno.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Rossi descrive così le priorità del presidente quando iniziò a lavorare alla Lazio: «Io ho avuto un presidente che non sapeva neanche se il pallone era rotondo o quadrato, quindi il suo obiettivo quando sono arrivato era risanare il bilancio e non mi ha chiesto neanche come giocassi, 4-3-3, 4-4-2, 3-5-2, che giocatori volessi, anche perché non c'avevamo soldi, quindi dovevamo prendere i giocatori che potevano capitare per cui il suo problema era quanto guadagnassi».

Alla domanda sul peso dell’ingaggio nella scelta dell’allenatore, Rossi risponde: «Se guadagnavo poco potevo essere un buon allenatore, se guadagnavo di più si rivolgeva da altre parti».

In a recent development, accanto al ricordo delle difficoltà economiche, Rossi esprime un giudizio netto sul lavoro societario di Lotito: «Ma devo dire che dal punto di vista societario ha fatto un lavoro incredibile alla Lazio perché ha risanato il bilancio. Noi eravamo una squadra che i giocatori-scommessa li dovevamo vendere per fare delle altre scommesse».

L’ex allenatore distingue le capacità del presidente dal rapporto personale: «Lotito è sicuramente una persona molto capace, intelligente e come carattere magari se dovevo andare a cena preferivo andarci con altri presidenti e non con lui».

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Making his Hoffenheim debut against Werder Bremen on 31 October, Natnael Abraha (18) has since earned rave reviews from managing director of football Andreas Schicker.

Just five days after playing the full 90 minutes against Bremen, Abraha completed another 90 minutes in Hoffenheim’s 1-1 draw in the UEFA Europa League at English Premier League’s Crystal Palace.

Recent findings suggest that “He has a great future ahead of him because he’s shown on the pitch what he brings to the table as a centre-back and right-back, both with and without the ball,” Schicker told Bild. “What I particularly like about him, though, is his humility, his down-to-earth nature, and his gratitude for being able to be part of the senior team. That’s why he received such an outstanding welcome from the team.”.

In training, Abraha has shown a willingness to learn. “Vladimír Coufal, also an extremely hard-working player and his direct competitor for the position, was practicing crosses after training. Natnael was passing him the balls,” explained Schicker, who lauded TSG’s rising star. “He observes carefully, how he crosses, how his standing foot is positioned, how he delivers the ball. He picked up quite a few things. That has to be emphasised, because nobody told him to do that, it came from him.

“It simply proves that the lad is down-to-earth and absolutely on the right track.”.

Recent findings suggest that born in Frankfurt, Abraha featured prominently for Germany’s U16 and U17 teams, bypassed the U18 squad and has earned six caps for the U19 squad after impressing for Hoffenheim II in the 3. Liga, where he’s made 18 appearances since January 2026.

Recent findings suggest that mario Vušković last played for Hamburg on 9 November 2022 but returned to action on Sunday afternoon after his four-year doping ban came to an end. Die Rothosen were playing in the 2. Bundesliga when the Croatian last played but to mark the occasion, the Bundesliga newcomers hosted a friendly against the defender’s former club, Hajduk Split, which was played in front of 50,000 supporters.

Recent findings suggest that “The last few days I was positively nervous and my mind was racing,” explained Vušković. “But it’s crazy how the brain works. When I was on the pitch, everything was normal again, like a training match and as if I’d been playing for the last four years.”.

Back in training for two months, Vušković has been working on his match fitness, and there’s a chance that he could be in HSV’s matchday squad for Sunday’s 111th Bundesliga Nordderby against Werder Bremen, as opposed to the second team.

In a recent development, “Our challenge now is to find a good mix,” explained head coach Merlin Polzin. “We will take the right steps together, step by step, so that he will once again be an key player for HSV in the long term.”.

Industry observers note that the script pretty much writes itself these days. A flicker of optimism and hope of a fresh start giving way to the same old frustrations, complaints and inquests, the cumulative toll of which places an ever greater strain on a club mired in mediocrity but with little reprieve from the expectations that come with bearing such an illustrious name.

Michael Carrick says Pro Ref’s apology over the derby fiasco means little to Manchester United – but warned his players they cannot allow such setbacks to derail their season.

Chief refereeing officer Howard Webb formally apologised to United after the VAR officials Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus failed to spot Enzo Fernandez was offside before wrongly allowing Erling Haaland’s winning goal to stand in Manchester City’s 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.

United were left shocked by the scale of the blunder, which came with 30 minutes of the game remaining and City already down to 10 men.

But Carrick has told his players not to become preoccupied with such injustices as they bid to overcome their poor start to the season before a crucial trip to Craven Cottage.

“It can have an impact in the moment of time, it can have a big impact, but we can’t let it have an impact on the rest of the season,” the United manager mentioned.

“That’s for us to get back to winning ways as soon as possible. Listen, one-off things can happen, at the time it was a pretty major one, we know that. I don’t think I need to go over that.

“But yeah, I’ve got faith in it [VAR], it’s the system that we work towards and that we use so the apology doesn’t mean an awful lot.”.

Carrick added: “I can appreciate and I respect it for them putting their hands up and saying we got that wrong, I think it happens - it does happen.

Industry observers note that “But moving forward, yeah, we just have to deal with it, what’s thrown in front of us. And maybe we get one or two decisions on the back of how it balances out - percentages or law of averages or whatever that may be.

“But that was a pretty major one to take and had a huge impact on that game and that’s why it was particularly tough.”.

Michael Carrick may have had a point when he said it was “ridiculous” to question his future this early in the season, but this afternoon’s game at Fulham will shape the mood at Manchester United for the next three weeks.

A tally of four points from their first four games of the season is a disappointing start, and Brighton added to the sense of gloom in the League Cup by becoming the first side in 50 years to win from 2-0 down at Old Trafford.

With Champions League football on the agenda, that competition was at the bottom of United’s priority list but the ragged nature of the performance prompted boos around the stadium.

The no-show at Hull and defeat to 10-man City also fall into the “it’s how you lose” category of defeat, while there are widening fissures between the fanbase and the club’s hierarchy over ticketing policy and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s political interventions.

In a recent development, the mood has also been sour at Fulham in the first few weeks of the season. In fact, they start the game bottom of the Premier League with one point, but do have the incentive of knowing a draw would take them above Spurs.

Following reports of friction between some established players and new head coach Alvaro Arbeloa though, they produced their best performance of the season in a goalless draw at Anfield last week when they had chances to win the game.

In a recent development, fulham made nine changes in the League Cup in mid-week, but still ran out 3-2 winners at West Ham. Despite the west London club being an established mid-table Premier League team for a number of seasons, and United’s vulnerable state for the past few years, Fulham have beaten their opponent’s just once in the league since December 2009.Full team news on the way shortly.

By LAWRENCE BOOTH, CRICKET CORRESPONDENT.

Published: 05:20 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 05:21 EST, 13 November 2026.

Pat Cummins is either the greatest actor in world sport – or the claim that the whole Australian team knew about the sandpaper plot in South Africa eight years ago is a figment of Usman Khawaja’s imagination.

After Cummins’s remarkable press conference in Sydney on Friday morning, in which he called Khawaja’s various assertions ‘complete and utter nonsense’ and questioned the validity of their friendship, it was hard to discern any common ground, much less spot a middle way.

According to the blue corner, everyone was in on the scam, sandpaper was used not just at Cape Town but in the previous Test at Port Elizabeth, and there was a team meeting to discuss the question of collective responsibility.

According to the red, those who knew about the plan did not include the bowlers, nothing untoward happened at Port Elizabeth, and there was no meeting.

Sources indicate that the only thing that can be mentioned for certain after another tumultuous 24 hours for Australian cricket was that the two corners are now polar opposites, each eyeing the other with suspicion and incredulity. Barring an improbable climbdown, the twain can never meet.

Industry observers note that cummins, it must be said, eased into his work after an emotional start behind a lectern at the Cricket Central venue in Sydney’s Olympic Park. He began by stating his basic position, then invited questions, which for the next hour and a bit he handled with aplomb and a degree of statesmanship.

Pat Cummins held a remarkable press conference in Sydney to address the sandpaper claims.

Speaking for more than an hour, Cummins dismissed Khawaja’s various assertions as ‘complete and utter nonsense’ and questioned the validity of their friendship.

This will not please those who still find it impossible to believe that Cummins and his fellow seamers on that trip, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc, knew nothing of the scheme that led to bans for three batsmen – Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft.

After all, as any bowler will tell you, the idea that the condition of their most prized possession might be altered without their noticing is as absurd as trying to persuade a batsman to walk out without his favourite willow.

And yet. Cummins stuck to his guns, in contrast to Khawaja’s appearance on the ABC on Wednesday evening, when he repeatedly declined to name Cummins as one of the guilty party. And while Khawaja reacted to his TV grilling by cancelling media engagements, Cummins made it clear he would be answering every question that came his way.

Whichever side you believe, and whatever the doubts that remain, his press conference grabbed the momentum from Team Khawaja.

It also made the previous day’s appearance by Mitchell Marsh, Australia’s white-ball captain for the next three weeks against England, all the more bizarre. By refusing to engage with any of the questions raised by Khawaja’s autobiography, Marsh – himself a veteran of South Africa 2018 – did little to dispel the suspicion that Khawaja had a point.

And that in turn encouraged the view that Cummins, who called his own press conference without the knowledge of Cricket Australia, might be about to come clean.

Instead, he doubled down on the denial he and his bowling colleagues had issued in 2021, but now went further, taking a clear-eyed and devastating aim at Khawaja’s integrity.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Usman is a friend, but friends aren’t casual with each other’s lives and reputations,’ said Cummins. ‘He’s dealt with the way he’s presented his story in a very casual manner and it affects a lot of people. That’s what I’m grappling with at the moment, because I don’t think that’s OK. It’s not what friends do.’.

Cummins plainly intended this to be his final word on the matter, but the problem facing Australian cricket is that the sore may never properly heal.

David Warner then hit back at Cummins and accused him of 'throwing Khawaja under the bus'.

Only a couple of hours after Cummins finished, Warner – at Perth’s Optus Stadium as a TV pundit for the first ODI between Australia and England – was being asked for his view, and he didn’t hold back, repeating his belief that Khawaja’s version of events was ‘the truth’.

He added: ‘I really, really support him. I actually feel for him at the moment. I feel that the captain today threw Uzzy under the bus and I’m very, very disappointed about that.’.

Industry observers note that disappointment. It’s mutual, and it’s everywhere. Cummins provided a brief distraction, but it doesn’t change the fact that this is a civil war with no obvious resolution.

Offered the chance to kick Australian cricket while it was down, England made humiliating contact with fresh air on the opening day of their eight-match white-ball trip.

Only hours after Pat Cummins had added a twist to the sandpaper saga by dismissing Usman Khawaja’s claims that the whole squad knew about the ball-tampering intends in South Africa eight years ago as ‘complete and utter nonsense’, Harry Brook’s side were blown away for 131 in the first ODI – having at one stage been 65 for eight.

Australia then romped home by seven wickets with more than 26 overs in hand to take a 1–0 lead into the second game of this three-match series in Adelaide on Sunday. For England, anyway, complete and utter nonsense felt about right.

It is not quite a year since they began their Ashes campaign here at the Optus Stadium by being bowled out in 32.5 overs in their first innings and 34.4 in their second – before stumbling to a 4–1 defeat.

Now, they obligingly split the difference, dismissed in 33.4 as Mahli Beardman, a 21-year-old fast bowler from Dunsborough, a couple of hours drive down the coast from Perth, picked up six for 34 – the best figures for Australia by an ODI debutant.

His first victim was Joe Root, caught behind for a painful 17 off 36 balls, and his second Brook, who had made only a single when he fidgeted fatally outside off stump.

That might have been enough to satisfy most newcomers, but Beardman had barely started. Jordan Cox made two before edging a poke, and Sam Curran top-edged a pull to fine leg for a duck.

When Liam Dawson, yet to score, squeezed a drive to backward point, Beardman had five wickets in 28 balls – not bad for a player whose only previous taste of international cricket had come in a T20 in Pakistan in January.

He then ended a lively last-wicket stand of 29 by removing Jofra Archer, who had just driven him down the ground for four. It was the only authentic boundary England managed off his bowling: the other, a streaky inside edge from Root, summed up the problems posed by his pace, bounce and accuracy. As bids for a place on next summer’s Ashes tour go, this was hard to ignore.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Laying in bed last night, that’s not what I had planned,’ said Beardman, who was taken under his wing by Australian fast-bowling legend Dennis Lillee after a mutual friend spotted him as a young teenager bowling at a bin down the side of a house. ‘It was an incredible game and it all happened so fast.’.

According to recent reports, if England had learned lessons from their collapses in the last year’s Test here, they revealed little sign of being able to implement them. Players drove on the up, as they had so heedlessly a year earlier, and failed to cope with the Perth bounce.

England head coach Brendon McCullum was critical of his side's failure to adapt to the pitch, and called on them to learn from their mistakes going forward.

Sources indicate that 'It’s a bit like batting on a trampoline,' mentioned McCullum. 'There are certain shots that are very difficult to execute. We talked about trying to put those away. We probably knew we were in for a low-scoring contest, but we expected to get a few more runs than 130.

'We're disappointed but there are some good lessons for us. If you look towards the World Cup in South Africa there’s going to be some pitches there that will test us from a bounce point of view.'.

And all this after they had played a warm-up game at the WACA – a grievous omission before the Ashes – and trained with such intensity that white-ball mentor Kevin Pietersen had declared it the best practice session he had seen from an England team.

In the event, their top-scorer was Gus Atkinson, who hit an unbeaten 29 from No 10, including England’s only six.

Mitchell Marsh, stroke-less in the previous day’s press conference, put that into perspective by clearing the ropes four times during a 29-ball half-century, while Cooper Connolly – dropped by Tom Banton at midwicket on five – hit two sixes himself.

According to recent reports, england’s only consolation had come at the start of Australia’s reply, when Atkinson bowled Travis Head first ball off the inside edge. Head it was who had taken care of Australia’s fourth-innings chase here a year ago, thrashing a 69-ball century that knocked the stuffing out of Ben Stokes’s attack.

Instead, it was Marsh who went for his shots, stopped only when he flicked Jamie Overton to Ben Duckett at deep midwicket, by which time Australia were already halfway there. For a few hours, at least, no one was talking about sandpaper.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Speaking ahead of the UEFA Nations League game against the Netherlands, German national team head coach Jürgen Klopp has called for a change in FIFA president.

Recent findings suggest that “The consensus now is that a change would make sense,” he explained, further noting that people who don’t have a financial interest should take over the leadership at football’s governing body. “People thought things couldn’t get any worse after Sepp Blatter, and then we got this. There are certainly people who care about football and have no financial interests. If one of them became president, it would be absolutely helpful,” he added.

Current FIFA president Gianni Infantino has come under fire recently, especially following the 2026 FIFA World Cup. European nations, along with member associations from CONCACAF and Asia, have asked for him to leave his role, despite Infantino still maintaining strong support from African federations.

Among the decisions that increased the pressure on Infantino were details that emerged of an aborted strategy to create a commercial company called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) to manage commercial interests and sell minority stakes in tournaments like the World Cup to private investors, including a private investor group led by Joshua Kushner’s firm Thrive Capital.

This has caused opposition from UEFA, CONCACAF, and the Asian Football Confederation – which accused Infantino of breaking trust “through deception” and acting above the collective.

Infantino’s close relationship with US President Donald Trump also created controversy, as the FIFA peace prize was awarded to Trump and Florian Balogun’s ban following a red card was lifted at the World Cup following a call with the US President.

Bayern Munich have announced that Alphonso Davies suffered a hamstring injury during the international break.

The 26-year-old lasted just six minutes of Canada’s 3-2 win in Guatemala on Saturday.

“Following a medical scan [Sunday] in Toronto, it has been confirmed that Alphonso Davies sustained a minor lower-body muscle strain. He is travelling back to Germany, where he will continue to receive ongoing care,” a Canada Soccer spokesperson informed Canadian Soccer Daily on Sunday evening.

Bayern have since confirmed that Davies will face time on the sidelines, even though a clear duration was not mentioned.

According to recent reports, according to Bayern Munich reporter for TZ, Philipp Kessler, Davies will be out for 7-10 days. The strategy is for him to return to the squad for the UEFA Champions League game in Lille next week, indicating that the injury isn’t serious.

Davies has struggled for consistent playing time in the last couple of seasons because of muscular injuries, and has also sustained hamstring injuries back in April and March, keeping him out of crucial games.

Why Man United staff feel treatment of Michael Carrick was 'disgusting' and the comment from Omar Berrada that raised eyebrows as club legend is put out of his misery - and Mauricio Pochettino gets set to take over

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1055 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 14:25 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:15 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino would have been fast asleep in his hotel room in the quirky American town of Trilith when Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox sat down with Michael Carrick at Carrington Thursday morning and confirmed the worst-kept secret in football.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 14:25 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:15 EST, 13 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino would have been fast asleep in his hotel room in the quirky American town of Trilith when Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox sat down with Michael Carrick at Carrington Thursday morning and confirmed the worst-kept secret in football.

It was time for Carrick to vacate the head coach’s office at Manchester United, and safe to say Pochettino will have his feet under the desk this time next week.

Carrick arrived at 7.50am but, unlike the last two days, he was no longer wearing his United training gear.

The agonising wait to be put out of his misery was over, and the club’s chief executive and director of football duly administered the last rites before Carrick left at 10.18am.

The decision was communicated to staff and Under-21s boss Adam Lawrence took training with the players who have remained at Carrington during the international break.

The first reports of Carrick’s sacking broke at 9.30am, but United insisted that they were premature and it wasn’t until 10.37am that the news was confirmed in a 142-word statement.

Michael Carrick finally left Carrington on Thursday morning after an agonising wait to be put out of his misery.

Staff at Manchester United believe that the former club captain's treatment at the hands of their Ineos paymasters has been 'disgusting'.

Recent findings suggest that it's understood that his backroom staff - assistant Steve Holland, coaches Jonathan Woodgate, Jonny Evans and Travis Binnion, and goalkeeper coach Craig Mawson - have also gone. When Evans left on Wednesday night with his car piled high with cardboard boxes, it didn't bode well.

Sources indicate that the treatment of Carrick and Evans, in particular, has upset staff. Two highly-respected figures at United, whose association with the club goes back more than 20 years, have been left hanging while their employers stumble over a succession plan.

Members of staff share Gary Neville’s view that Berrada and Wilcox meeting with Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco, and making a move for Pochettino while Carrick had to keep driving past the cameras on his way into Carrington for the last three days, was ‘disgusting’.

It has also reignited anger over the 450 job cuts carried out by Ratcliffe and Ineos over the past three years while pouring millions down the drain in compensation.

The £10million to buy Pochettino and his staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation, and the pay-off owing to Carrick and Co, will push the cost of hiring and firing coaches in the Ineos era close to £50m.

No wonder eyebrows were raised when Berrada spoke at Sir Alex Ferguson’s 40th anniversary dinner at Old Trafford on Friday night and talked about building a culture at the club.

The feeling is that changing United’s head coach won’t make a shred of difference if there isn’t significant change higher up the chain.

It has once again turned the spotlight on the relationship between Ratcliffe and the Glazer family, who from February can force him to sell his 28 per cent holding to a third party for less than the £25-per-share he paid in 2024 unless he can match the offer and buy the club himself.

However, United sources say they had little choice but to sack Carrick with the club in the relegation zone, having decided to give him a stay of execution at the end of last month.

Since then, the club had carried out a comprehensive review and come to the conclusion that a record of one win from 10 Premier League games was unacceptable.

The sources indicated that the United board shared the frustration and anger felt by fans over the situation, and believe that a change of head coach will bring about an improvement from a squad that is far better than results would suggest.

While United praised Carrick for his ‘highest degree of professionalism’, there was only silence from the players on social media.

Many of them are on international duty, including Bruno Fernandes whose criticism of Carrick’s tactics after the Champions League defeat to Como proved so damaging.

Following the announcement of Carrick's dismissal none of his former players - including Bruno Fernandes - were quick to say their goodbyes publicly.

Meanwhile, his would-be successor Mauricio Pochettino is set to face the media on Friday.

Pochettino will inherit this squad of players once he has completed his duties as US national team coach with the upcoming CONCACAF Nations League double-header against Haiti.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss is due to speak at 2.15pm Friday ahead of the first leg in Miami on Saturday night when he will face questions over the United job for the first time.

Pochettino is expected to stay in charge for the second leg in Cincinnati in the early hours of Wednesday morning before flying to Manchester to meet the players and prepare for the crunch clash with Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

The US have been staying in Trilith, near their upcoming training headquarters in Fayetteville south-west of Atlanta, where they were also based before the World Cup.

According to recent reports, it’s a unique place designed for the film industry and built around the Trilith Studios which are the largest outside Hollywood. The ideal place for Pochettino to prepare for life at Old Trafford.

He has embraced the American lifestyle since he was appointed US coach in September 2024, a few months after leaving Chelsea, and will be sorry to leave.

Pochettino is remarked to have developed a love of bourbon whiskey, country music and Nashville, with Ella Langley’s Choosin’ Texas one of his favourite tunes.

He has admitted crying over Miracle, the movie about the US hockey team made up of college kids famously beating the Soviet Union to the gold medal at the 1980 Winter Olympics.

But the pull of Manchester United was always going to be too great, and very soon he will be swapping Trilith for Old Trafford.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in un articolo de l'Equipe si parla di Andy Diouf e della sua ultima apparizione con la Francia, nella vittoria contro la Turchia. Sotto la lente di ingrandimento del giornale francese finisce il modo di marcare del calciatore dell'Inter che Zidane schiera come terzino sinistro, in un ruolo che non è suo.

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

"Fin dall'inizio della partita, Andy Diouf (in campo per tutta la durata dell'incontro) si è occupato di marcare Abdülkerim Bardakci. La Francia si è difes a uomo aggiungendo dei giocatori in marcatura a zona come ad esempio Rabiot e Barcola vicino al primo palo quando c'erano i calci d'angolo. Gli incarichi di Zidane erano chiari. Ma fin dal primo calcio d'angolo la marcatura del giocatore dell'Inter sul suo uomo si allenterà. La squadra turca batterà il corner corto. Dopo i primi due passaggi, Diouf sarà l'unico ad aver perso il suo marcatore. Quando il pallone verrà crossato in area, Bardakci e un compagno avranno una superiorità numerica in fase di ricezione contro Jacquet, che riuscirà a procurarsi il fallo. Primo segnale d'allarme", si legge nell'articolo.

Che continua sulla partita del giocatore nerazzurro: "Sedici minuti dopo Diouf è stato lento a reagire all'inserimento di Bardakci. Al 60esimo minuto, un altro calcio d'angolo, il difensore centrale turco era lì per colpire di testa ma ha mancato il pallone. Diouf era troppo lontano. Non è la prima volta che il giocatore, che sta scoprendo il ruolo di terzino sinistro con i Bleus, si trova in questa situazione. Già al secondo minuto della sua prima apparizione, in Belgio il 28 settembre, l'ex giocatore del Lens aveva perso nettamente la marcatura su Ngoy".

(Screenshot da tv francese da l'Equipe).

Sources indicate that E quindi poi è arrivato il gol del due a uno con Andy Diouf che ha perso di vista ancora Bardakci e arriva il gol. "Al momento del calcio d'angolo, si ripresentano gli schemi di marcatura visti dall'inizio della partita. Konaté su Demiral (numero 3), Jacquet su Gül (19), Da Cunha su Topçu (4), Kumbedi su Özcan (5), il sostituto di Yüksek. Tutti sono pronti tranne Diouf.Non può far altro che guardare Bardakci, solo a prendere la palla, battere Restes da distanza ravvicinata", scrive ancora l'Equipe.

Recent findings suggest that il giornale francese poi parla di come invece il francese gioca nell'Inter: "Andy Diouf non si trova mai in una situazione del genere. La squadra allenata da Cristian Chivu difende sui calci d'angolo a zona, non a uomo. Pertanto, il tecnico rumeno e il suo staff tendono a tenere il francese lontano dalle zone più pericolose da cui riceve il pallone. Con la nazionale francese, è stato addirittura esonerato dalla marcatura a uomo in due dei quattro calci d'angolo concessi contro il Belgio (tra casa e trasferta). Finché non migliorerà, questo potrebbe essere la soluzione migliore".

According to recent reports, anche il direttore sportivo dell'Ascoli Matteo Patti è stato premiato quest'oggi ad Arezzo nel corso del Gran Galà del Calcio e ai microfoni di TMW ha ripercorso l'ultimo anno e mezzo spiegando l'idea alla base della costruzione della squadra: “L'idea dello scorso anno era quella di costruire una squadra giovane, che potesse fare bene e compiere un percorso duraturo all'interno dell'Ascoli. Adesso ci troviamo in Serie B, stiamo facendo abbastanza bene e sicuramente stiamo bruciando qualche tappa, ma siamo solo all'inizio e non possiamo dire di averle bruciate, ma è un buon inizio".

Si aspettava questo avvio? "Non mi aspettavo il terzo posto, non ci aspettavamo questo avvio come risultati e classifica, ma come prestazioni sì perché siamo convinti che i nostri giocatori e il nostro mister possono fare bene e ambire a consolidarsi in questa categoria".

State già guardando al mercato? "È normale, oggi è tutto talmente veloce chi bisogna stare sempre sul pezzo e attenti alle opportunità di mercato che possono presentarsi, stiamo lavorando e vagliando tutte le possibilità".

Industry observers note that siete felici di D'Uffizi convocato dall'Under 21? "Siamo contentissimi di Simone, si è meritato la convocazione in Under 21 dopo essersi costruito tutto un percorso, non gli abbiamo regalato nulla e lui si è conquistato quello che ha oggi. Ci auguriamo che abbia un futuro roseo e magari con l'Ascoli”.
