Manchester City found guilty of 114 charges

📅 25 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2088 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules.
  • Recent findings suggest that city face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League.
  • If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules. It is a decision that, if upheld, would equate to one of the biggest scandals in football history.

Recent findings suggest that city face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League. Or a combination of all, under rule W51 of its handbook. No punishment has yet been unveiled.

If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.

The charges can be broken down into five categories and relate to a period from 2009-23 in which City won six League Cups, three FA Cups, seven league titles and the Champions League. There is the provision for removing past titles, but that would appear remote.

City have been the dominant force in English football for most of that time, but that status is under threat with a verdict that will send shockwaves around Europe and could have huge ramifications for the club.

That is unless they can win an appeal, with sources cautioning it still may take up to another two to three years for the case to be resolved, following on from an already five-year investigation.

The Premier League’s rules provide for an independent appeal board with broad powers, including the ability to uphold, vary or overturn the independent commission’s decision.

Industry observers note that it would therefore appear that despite the verdict, the case is far from being resolved and punishment decided. The details of the commission’s findings, when published, will be crucial to determining what happens next.

But if it is upheld, the verdict also opens up the possibility of City facing legal action from other clubs who feel they missed out on trophies and even merit money from league placings.

It is understood Premier League clubs are already discussing legal action and possible compensation claims as a result of the guilty verdict.

Sources indicate that each of those cases would have to be held individually, potentially leading to years more of litigation. Conversely, if City win their appeal, they too could take legal action against the Premier League the damage caused to their reputation.

There has not yet been an official confirmation of the independent panel’s verdict from the Premier League. The Premier League declined to comment.

However, several sources have told Telegraph Sport that the panel has found City guilty of all but one of the charges they faced. The one that has not been proved is mentioned to be one of the most serious of the 115.

The damning verdict for City is a major fresh test of fragile UK relations with the United Arab Emirates, with whom bilateral trade was worth £25bn last year. Redacted freedom of information documents, seen by Telegraph Sport, show Abu Dhabi hosted UK government officials including Lord Stockwood, then investment minister, as recently as February. Khaldoon Al Mubarak, the City chairman and trusted adviser to the UAE president, was present at the meeting. Government notes from the meeting recorded that he “noted they are very proud of what they have achieved through their investments in Manchester”.

Sources indicate that the Government previously caused acrimony among senior leaders in Abu Dhabi after putting forward legislation to ban foreign states from owning UK newspapers and news magazines. The intervention prompted the collapse of a takeover of The Telegraph in April 2024, which was largely funded by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the owner of City and vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates.

Industry observers note that the previous UK government has admitted its embassy in Abu Dhabi and the Foreign Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) in London discussed the charges levelled at City by the Premier League. However it refused to disclose the correspondence.

City have steadfastly maintained they are innocent, promising “irrefutable” evidence in support of their position, and had assembled some of the most expensive lawyers in the country to argue their case. Despite the verdict, the club are understood to be confident that it will win the argument in the end. Senior figures are said to be calm about the latest development, as significant as it seems.

City rebuilt their team this summer and it is understood that signings were brought in on conventional player contracts, rather than terms including clauses triggered in the event of a heavy punishment. Given the club have consistently denied breaching financial regulations, and their deals for new players to work with head coach Enzo Maresca underlines their position.

On Friday, a City spokesman stated: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

“The club have diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”.

Sources close to Pep Guardiola, the former City manager who stepped down last summer after 10 years of remarkable success at the club, including a treble triumph in 2023 and an unprecedented fourth straight league title in 2024, insist he has not been informed of any verdict.

In the days after City were first charged, Guardiola mounted a fierce defence of the club, claiming: “I am fully convinced we will be [proved] innocent.”.

The verdict vindicates the Premier League’s decision to launch an investigation after explosive allegations that City had routinely broken financial rules were first made in Der Spiegel in 2018 based on the Football Leaks documents.

Uefa previously accused City of breaches of its financial regulations and declared in 2020 that it was suspending the club from the Champions League for two years for “overstating” sponsorship revenue between 2012 and 2016.

City denied the Uefa charges and, after an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, the two-year ban was overturned. Cas found that a number of the claims brought by Uefa had fallen outside a five-year “time bar” and others were “not established”.

Industry observers note that it did, however, still impose a €10m fine after ruling that City failed to cooperate with investigators. City had previously also agreed a settlement with Uefa of €20m in 2014 following an investigation into their finances.

Legal experts agreed that the commission’s verdict is far from the end of the case. Yasin Patel, barrister at Church Court Chambers, remarked: “City’s lawyers will now analyse this decision and look at the options open to them to appeal, which may include procedural impropriety, wrongful interpretation of law, and legal errors – importantly, they can guarantee an appeal.

Recent findings suggest that “Sanctions could include a major fine, points deduction, relegation or even all three. Factoring in whether titles and trophies should be stripped, whether other clubs have been robbed of further revenue and opportunities due to City’s wrongdoings and losses incurred, we safely say that this is only the first chapter of a long-running legal saga that will not end any time soon.”.

Ian Hargreaves, partner with specialist disputes firm Quillon Law, stated the verdict was “not the end of the story but the beginning of a fresh phase”, and added: “There is also the question of whether the panel’s decision can withstand a hard-fought appeal, and on what grounds any challenge might be brought. Much will depend on the detail of the panel’s findings and reasoning, which will inevitably be closely scrutinised by both sides.”.

Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri, who won the Ballon d’Or during his trophy-laden spell at the club, stated he believed the club were innocent.

“For the players, it’s different than it is for journalists. I can understand all opinions, but we try to stay positive,” the Spain midfielder stated while on international duty.

Industry observers note that “When you see all the people who worked hard at City to achieve success, you know what we achieved can’t be taken away. It wasn’t paid for with money, but with effort and teamwork. Everything we achieved was deserved; we marked one of the great eras of English football. I believe in the club’s innocence – we already went through this in 2020.”.

Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister, remarked: “I think we would all need to study the independent commission’s report in some considerable detail before reaching any conclusions.”.

Zohran Kwame Mamdani, the mayor of Upcoming York, posted “114” in relation to the charges while former Manchester United players David de Gea and Rio Ferdinand both asked whether they should be due winner’s medals from past seasons.

Industry observers note that the Premier League statement in February 2023 remarked that “a number of alleged breaches” had been referred to an independent commission. It then detailed each specific rule against each season in which the alleged breach took place. The precise number was not clear from the statement and led to varying reports between 115 and 130. Friday’s news suggested the figure was 115.

In a recent development, all the way to 2009-10, the first full season following the club’s takeover by Sheikh Mansour, who is a member of the Abu Dhabi Royal family and the vice president of the United Arab Emirates. There were charges relating to all 14 seasons until the Premier League completed their investigation during the 2022-23 campaign. In that time, City won seven Premier League titles, six League Cups, three FA Cups and the Champions League. They have since won another league title – the first club to do so four times in a row – as well as the Uefa Super Cup, the Fifa Club World Cup and the FA Cup and League Cup double last season.

Sources indicate that they can be split into five groups. The biggest relates to the seasons from 2009-10 until 2017-18 and the requirement for clubs to provide accurate financial information and act in the utmost good faith.

The next set of rules concern the full disclosure of manager and player payments. The alleged manager breaches related to the period between 2009-10 and 2012-13, when Roberto Mancini was leading the team. The alleged breaches with respect to player payments relate to all of the seasons between 2010-11 and 2015-16.

According to recent reports, as well as providing financial detail, clubs were required to meet Uefa and Premier League rules which were designed to bring a club’s spending broadly in line with their income by placing set limits on losses. City were charged with breaches of Uefa’s licencing and financial fair play rules from 2013-14 until 2017-18, and the Premier League’s profit and sustainability rules from 2015-16 until 2017-18.

The final set of charges spanned the five seasons during which City were being investigated by the Premier League and rules that require members to cooperate in the utmost good faith by providing information and documents.

In a recent development, A full picture will only emerge when the commission publishes its findings but we know that the Premier League investigation began in December 2018 following allegations in the German newspaper Der Spiegel based on the Football Leaks documents. These included alleged payments to former manager Mancini for consultancy work at an Abu Dhabi-based club that was separate to his regular contract at City.

Sources indicate that we also know that City were alleged to have breached rules over setting out image rights payments to players in their club contract. Der Spiegel reported that the Premier League investigation also focused on payments to under-age players, as well as whether club sponsors were paying for commercial deals themselves or a significant proportion was in fact effectively coming from owner Sheikh Mansour.

City have always denied breaking any rules. In response to the Premier League statement about the alleged breaches, they said that they have “irrefutable evidence” to support their position and “look forward to this matter being put to rest once and for all.”.

Industry observers note that at the start of the hearing in September 2024, Guardiola also remarked: “Wait for the independent panel. We believe we have not done anything wrong.”.

Of the Football Leaks documents, City stated: “We will not be providing any comment on out-of-context materials. The attempt to damage the club’s reputation is organised and clear.”.

France star Desire Doue was left with a loose front tooth after being hit with a nasty elbow in France's 3-1 defeat to Italy in the Nations League.

The PSG winger was left in need of some emergency dental work by Italy's Davide Frattesi who caught the 21-year-old in the mouth while shielding the ball.

According to recent reports, in his post match interview French boss Zinedine Zidane, when asked if Doue had lost a tooth, replied: 'Yeah I think so. We’re going to take him straight there, a tooth has come loose I think, we’ll take care of him starting tomorrow.'.

It was a poor day all round for the Frenchman who not only had his tooth dislodged but was also unable to impact a poor game for Les Blues in which the Azzuri beat them at the San Siro.

To compound Doue's misery it was the offender Frattesi who scored Italy's second goal in the 3-1 win just six minutes before he performed some unorthodox dentistry.

The Lazio midfielder's goal completed the Italians' comeback after going 1-0 down to a Michael Olise goal just ten minutes in before Inter Milan's Francesco Esposito levelled things up just 16 minutes later.

Desire Doue was left with a loose front tooth after receiving an elbow in the mouth from Davide Fratessi.

Fratessi got away with just a yellow card as Italy beat the French 3-1 at the San Siro.

Frattesi gave Italy the lead early on in the second half before Esposito netted his second from the spot to put the game out of reach.

Speaking after the game Zidane was surprisingly positive about his team's performance despite the loss, saying that losing is, 'part of the process.'.

The French then went onto say: 'The most crucial thing is creating chances. Hitting the post had an impact, but I'm not disappointed.

Sources indicate that 'I would have been if we hadn't created good possession. What we need to analyse is why we weren't at the right level off the ball.'.

The World Cup winner was not entirely positive however, later saying: 'in the second half we ran into difficulties, especially defensively.'.

The victory put Italy level on points with the French in Group A with both sides having won three drawn one and lost one.

But France will have an opportunity to right their wrongs and return to the top of the group on Sunday as they welcome Turkey.

But if Italy beat Belgium on the same day the French will have to settle for second.

Scotland’s ramped-up second-half performance offered some cause for optimism as Sébastien Pocognoli’s tenure as head coach began with a goalless draw with Slovenia in Ljubljana.

The 39-year-old Belgian head coach, appointed in August as Steve Clarke’s successor, refreshed the side for the Nations League Group B1 opener in the Stozice Stadium, but they were fortunate on a couple of occasions at least not to fall behind before rallying before the break.

Scotland had been insipid and uninspiring for most of the first half but after the interval they played with pace and purpose as Slovenia captain and goalkeeper Jan Oblak became a key figure, making saves from Oli McBurnie and Kieron Bowie.

Oli McBurnie spurns a chance for Scotland.It remains goalless between Slovenia and Scotland.📺 Watch on BBC One pic.twitter.com/sldzhNCGGb.

“It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play,” McBurnie told BBC Scotland.

“We created enough chances to win the game. I should have scored. I was asked to play a different position and I enjoyed it. I’d rather be getting in the positions than not getting chances.

It has been revealed that “Second half was a lot more of what the manager wanted from us. It was waves of pressure and the only thing missing was a goal or two.”.

However, the goal that would have made the former Union Saint-Gilloise and Monaco manager’s debut as an international boss more memorable ultimately failed to arrive.

In this extended international break, the Scots will host Switzerland at Hampden on Tuesday and then travel to North Macedonia before taking on Slovenia in Glasgow, with the Tartan Army hoping to see further improvement – and goals.

September 29: Scotland vs Switzerland.

October 3: North Macedonia vs Scotland.

October 6: Scotland vs Slovenia.

November 13: Scotland vs North Macedonia.

November 16: Switzerland vs Scotland.

Speaking to BBC Scotland, the debutant remarked: “Thought we struggled to get into the game first half, but second half we completely dominated the game.

Sources indicate that “They’ve got a top goalie who made really good saves. So many positives to take and a clean sheet as well.

“We changed shape a wee bit at half-time to get more control and that did really well for us.

“It’s a substantial game again on Tuesday so it’s key to recover now and go again.

“I’ve played on the left-hand side for a couple of years now, so I’m comfortable doing that.

In a recent development, “We’ve had a great week. A latest manager, new way of playing and new faces in camp. It’s just the chances we need to take - the fact we’re creating the chances stands us in good stead.”.

The striker told BBC Scotland: “It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play.

The hosts make their fifth alteration of the afternoon, with Cerin withdrawn and Lovric on instead.

The ball is then delivered into the box toward McGinn, whose header bounces off McBurnie. Hickey is arriving to pounce on the loose ball, but the wing-back’s effort is blocked by the Slovenian defence.

In a recent development, robertson picks up the game’s first yellow card for an off-the-ball incident. The Scotland captain is clearly very unhappy with the decision as we await to see a replay. Nevertheless, the action resumes with a Slovenia free-kick.

Slovenia go close again as a corner is whipped in. Drkusic wins the header at the near post and it bounces off the outside of the near post. That is definitely another warning sign for Scotland.

Matko goes on the outside of Welsh, and from a tight angle, he shoots, but his fizzed effort saves the side netting of the near post. Some fans behind the goal cheer because they think it’s gone in, but their view has really deceived them.

Sources indicate that it’s been a quiet afternoon for both goalkeepers so far, with neither yet to make a noteworthy save. On a couple of occasions, Slovenia have had encouraging opportunities to get the ball into the Scotland’s box, but the deliveries have been overhit and poorly executed.

Similarly to Scotland, Slovenia are also playing a tremendously high-line. Unlike Slovenia, Scotland have been unable to find the right pass in behind the home side’s defence. Gilmour then carelessly gives the ball away as Scotland’s latest spell of possession ends.

Since Slovenia wasted that 14th-minute chance, Scotland have grown into the contest and are beginning to look comfortable in possession. However, they’re still waiting to craft their first notable opening here.

According to recent reports, the hosts miss a huge chance! Once again, Sturm gets in behind Scotland’s incredibly high line and then fires a low cross into the penalty area. Sporar then beats McKenna to the delivery, but taps his close-range effort wide of the far post from inside the six-yard box. That’s a massive let-off for Scotland...

In a recent development, matko is unleashed by a drilled pass then pierces through a gap between Robertson and Welsh. The Slovenia winger drives into the penalty area and tries to find either Sturm or Sporar with a cross, but Hendry does magnificently to make a last-ditch clearance.

Sources indicate that slovenia have the ball in the net, but the offside flag is up. Sturm gets in behind Scotland’s defence and slides a low cross into Sporar’s path. The striker then sweeps a composed first-time effort into the top corner. It’s a brilliant finish, but Sturm was miles offside in the build-up.

Industry observers note that gunn comes out confidently to collect a looping cross, before the ball is launched forward in McBurnie’s direction. The Hull City striker and Ure are playing really close to each other, very much like an old-school front-two.

Sources indicate that slovenia forward Sturm is wiped out by Hendry’s wild early challenge. The Scotland defender is perhaps lucky to avoid a booking. Welsh then heads the resulting set-piece away and out for a corner.

The hosts get us underway in the Slovenian capital. Can Pocognoli begin his Scotland tenure with a Nations League victory?

Recent findings suggest that both teams are out on the pitch in Ljubljana. We are moments away from the start of the Pocognoli era.

Angus Gunn remains his country’s first-choice goalkeeper.

“The first game is always a special game so you have to bring the mental aspect in for the players and for the staff.

“A good result can help but the most crucial thing is we see things that we work on through the week. I hope is we apply that well then we will get the result which will be the perfect mix.

Industry observers note that “I hope we can bring a good game, and a good exciting principle on the pitch. I think we need the support from the supporters because there’s a lot of new players.

“We need to create a good energy but it’s up to us on the pitch to create this. So then we can be hand in hand with the supporters.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this UEFA Nations League B, Group 1 match as Slovenia host Scotland at Stozice Stadium in Ljubljana.

Scotland qualified for their first World Cup in 28 years this summer, but they exited the tournament with a whimper after failing to finish as one of the best third-place group sides. Steve Clarke’s men beat tournament debutants Haiti 1-0 in their opening match, before falling to defeats without scoring against Morocco and Brazil.

Following the World Cup, Clarke stepped down as Scotland’s head coach, ending a seven-year tenure, and was replaced by Belgian manager Sebastien Pocognoli. The former Monaco boss will take charge of his first game in his fresh role today and will be itching to make an encouraging start in a new era for Scottish football.

Over this extended international break, Pocognoli’s side will also face Switzerland and North Macedonia, as well as a return fixture against Slovenia in Scotland on October 6 to round off a busy period.

While Scotland took part in the World Cup, Slovenia were reflecting on their hugely disappointing qualification performance, where they finished third in their group behind Switzerland and Kosovo without winning and netting just three goals across six matches.

Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko – Slovenia’s star man and most well-known player – withdrew from Bostjan Cesar’s squad earlier this week after the recurrence of a shin injury caused the 23-year-old to completely miss the 1-1 draw against Fulham last Sunday.

Scotland have a few notable absences, with Scott McTominay, Che Adams and Lawrence Shankland all unavailable, but Billy Gilmour returns to the fold after missing the World Cup through injury, Oli McBurnie has been recalled and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure has received his first senior call-up.

Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news coming shortly.

#2752. Tech Report: Why England were unremarkable on Harry Kane's big night, the Ben White problem - and established star whose place could be under threat from Morgan Rogers, writes IAN LADYMAN

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1605 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Why England were unremarkable on Harry Kane's big night, the Ben White problem - and established star whose place could be under threat from Morgan Rogers, writes IAN LADYMAN

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1605 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 07:49 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • According to recent reports, england will head to Spain on Sunday for a Nations League shoot out with the World Champions.
  • It wasn't always easy on Harry Kane's massive night at Wembley against Croatia, though.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By IAN LADYMAN, FOOTBALL EDITOR.

Published: 02:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 07:49 EST, 13 November 2026.

According to recent reports, england will head to Spain on Sunday for a Nations League shoot out with the World Champions. A win in Madrid could see Thomas Tuchel's team progress to the quarter-finals next March as group winners.

It wasn't always easy on Harry Kane's massive night at Wembley against Croatia, though. Indeed this was probably England's worst performance since losing to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final last July.

Here Daily Mail Sport looks at the key issues emerging from last night's tight squeeze.

Self-defeating abuse of White is madness and must stop.

In case nobody has noticed, England are not over stocked with competent right-backs.

Trent Alexander-Arnold isn't wholly trusted in significant games by Thomas Tuchel, Reece James is always injured and Tino Livramento has also struggled to be available. Why, then, is a significant section of the England support so determined to drive Ben White away from the international scene?

According to recent reports, white plays for Arsenal, the champions of England. He is a fine, versatile defender who would be gratefully received and appreciated by fans of most national teams in world football. He had challenges with the previous England management regime and does not apologise for that.

It has been revealed that ben White was booed when he came on. The abuse towards the defender must stop.

Recent findings suggest that he spoke about it this week and made it clear he didn't wish to reopen old wounds. All that matters now is that he is willing and available. But – despite a plea from Tuchel before this game – England fans still booed him when he came on as a substitute last night.

It's a disgraceful way to treat a footballer who can be an asset to his country going forwards and it's something the England manager cares deeply about. Do we want to win the next Euros or not? Do we want our best players motivated and driven and part of the squad? Or do we want to faff about harbouring old grudges related to a situation in Qatar four winters ago that none of us really know that much about?

The choice is clear. If we are not careful, we will drive a good footballer away from the England set-up for good. It's madness.

Significant night for Kane but questions for England.

They came to celebrate Harry Kane and the England captain got his goal. Number 92 for the striker. Beneath all the fuss over England's talisman, however, this came perilously close to being a step backwards for Thomas Tuchel's England.

Recent findings suggest that the England manager has been saying since the last international break in September and October that he wanted his team to go to Madrid on Sunday in with a shout at knocking Spain from the top of this Nations League Group. Had Croatia been a little smarter in front of goal at Wembley last night, England would have been heading for a dead rubber against the world champions.

Harry Kane scored on his big night as England edged out a 2-1 win over Croatia at Wembley.

It was a night to remember for Kane as he was honoured after receiving his record 126th cap.

It has been revealed that three times in the last ten minutes of this game, Croatia had good opportunities to score a second goal and take a point from the game that would have been perfectly justified. So England crawled over the line but there was little here that was impressive with questions emerging once again about how capable really are when they don't have the ball.

Kane put it well himself afterwards when he said: 'You can't always expect things to be perfect. Of course, we know we can improve on a few bits and we will need to if we want to win on Sunday.'.

It has been revealed that tuchel himself will perhaps have quiet concerns. One of the German's worries about this England team is that they sometimes struggle to take training performances on to the field and this was another case in point.

The ultimate target for this team is to win the home Euros in 2028 and the pressure will need handling in front of their own supporters if they are to do that. With that in mind, it's good to know that the FA are interested in hosting the finals of this Nations League competition next summer.

If England make it through next March's two-legged quarter-finals, they could do with some practice of playing high-stakes games at Wembley.

Asked last week on the day he announced his squad whether Jordan Pickford was still his number one goalkeeper, Tuchel was unequivocal.

'He is,' said Tuchel. 'But the competition is on there as well. Like for the outfield players. And James Trafford will get regular starts now, that's what we wanted. They shared the matches last time. There's an opportunity that we maybe do this again.'.

Morgan Rogers impressed after opening the scoring inside the opening half-an-hour.

Jordan Pickford starting against Croatia could lead to James Trafford playing against Spain.

It has been revealed that with all this in mind, it was expected that Trafford would start this game with Pickford getting the gloves for the one that really matters in Spain on Sunday. That wasn't the case, so we wait with interest to see what the England manager does in Madrid.

What nobody really wants is for a return to the situation we had in the 1980s when Ron Greenwood used to rotate between the late Ray Clemence and last night's guest of honour Peter Shilton.

Industry observers note that england's back four is the one area of this team that can look unconvincing – they did again last night - and the last thing they need is not to know who their goalkeeper is from one match to the next. Tuchel is going to have to make a decision.

Interesting that Tuchel chose to put Dan Burn into his team for this game, despite the Newcastle defender not being in the original squad.

With Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa both absent with injuries, Everton's Jarrod Branthwaite would have expected to play on the left of Jarell Quansah here. Instead, Burn leapfrogged him in the queue and maybe we should have paid more attention to something Tuchel remarked the day before the game.

'Jarrad Branthwaite is doing very well but it's a very different style of play for him from Everton towards us,' stated Tuchel.

Jarrad Branthwaite clearly has a way to go before he's fully trusted to start by Thomas Tuchel.

Industry observers note that 'You can see that Dan Burn is straight away a big voice in training and is more used to the style with Newcastle from the last two seasons with Eddie Howe where they followed in a high press and to man-man. And of course he was with us at the World Cup so he is used a bit more to our style of play.'.

It has been revealed that that's all very well and logical but – that being the case – why was Branthwaite chosen ahead of Burn in the original group of 25 last Friday? Burn, as it happened, had a very good game last night.

In a recent development, tuchel talks always about the value of players being in camp. 'The train is leaving the station,' is one of the England manager's more memorable quotes of recent times. Players like Cole Palmer, for example, have learned to their cost that missing meet-ups with injuries can be costly.

Bukayo Saka is not in that category and has plenty of credit in the bank with the England manager. However, Tuchel's fondness for Morgan Rogers is well known and Saka's absence does give him a way of getting the Chelsea player into his team. Rogers may be a number ten at heart but he was effective once again here out on the right side.

The 24-year-old was one of England's better players on a muted night against Croatia and he deserved his first half goal. He gives England a more direct, athletic dimension on the opposite flank to the more balletic offerings of Anthony Gordon. Food for thought for Tuchel at least as Saka continues his own battle against persistent injuries.

Bukayo Saka's long-term place in England's team could be under threat from Morgan Rogers.

United should have moved for Hall.

It has been revealed that newcastle United were pretty much an open door in the summer as they sold players left right and centre. Gordon to Barcelona to make sure the club was the right side of the financial guidelines and then Sandro Tonali to Tottenham and Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal simply because the players made it known they wanted to go.

Strange, then, that Manchester United didn't make a proper move for left-back Lewis Hall. Admittedly this wasn't the most difficult match in which he will have ever played, but Hall was impressive once again.

With Luke Shaw so injury prone, Hall pretty much has the left-back berth sewn up for England but it feels as though he now needs to make the next step in his club career. United retain a nominal interest but who knows what incoming manager Mauricio Pochettino may think? It's hard to work out why United didn't try harder to sign him last summer. He has subsequently signed a newly introduced contract at Newcastle, of course.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, il presidente del Lecce, Saverio Sticchi Damiani, ha parlato a margine del "Premio Modello Virtuoso del Calcio Italiano", intitolato a Italo Galbiati. Ecco le sue parole raccolte da TuttoMercatoWeb.com: "L'idea di puntare molto sul settore giovanile e quindi una politica sui giovani è l'unico modo per rendere sostenibile il club. Ci stiamo lavorando da anni; solo due-tre anni fa, abbiamo vinto un titolo Primavera di cui siamo molto orgogliosi. E adesso sono anche contento che la nostra Primavera sta portando nella squadra Under 20 tanti ragazzi che vengono dalle trafile del settore giovanile, quindi tanti ragazzi salentini. Un processo che mi piace molto, anche perché la Primavera sta facendo particolarmente bene".

According to recent reports, sul campionato: chiaro che ci vuole un po' di sofferenza, ma siete abituati per centrare la permanenza in A. Come giudica questa prima parte di stagione in generale? "Un inizio di stagione in linea un po' con quello che era il nostro percorso. Forse quello che è un po' inaspettato sono i così tanti infortuni che abbiamo avuto quest'anno: non mi era mai capitato in 11 anni da presidente del club di avere così tanti giocatori importanti infortunati, alcuni dello stesso ruolo. Però abbiamo affrontato l'emergenza e chi è subentrato ha fatto anche il massimo, però un prezzo per quello l'abbiamo pagato. Nonostante tutto la squadra ha 10 punti e oggi è in una posizione buona di classifica, ma ovviamente dobbiamo recuperare gli infortunati e cercare di fare meglio".

It has been revealed that nota un livello che si è alzato verso l'alto per inseguire l'obiettivo della salvezza? "Si è alzato il livello ed è cambiato anche il tipo di gestione della partita: quest'anno le partite hanno un tempo effettivo molto più alto, uno sforzo fisico più importante rispetto al passato, [quando] c'erano tante interruzioni e il tempo effettivo era molto più basso. Forse anche questo è il motivo dei tanti infortuni, perché ho visto che non è un problema solo del Lecce, ma è piuttosto diffuso. Quindi, almeno sul piano atletico, si è complicato tutto e devo dire il livello generale si è alzato".

Sarà sempre Eusebio Di Francesco il vostro top player? Ha un allenatore molto bravo che l'anno scorso ha centrato la salvezza e quest'anno ha cambiato anche un po' modo di giocare a calcio, con un Lecce anche un po' più "giochista" rispetto al passato, no? "Sì, l'intenzione era quella. Poi c'è da dire che forse un po' le caratteristiche proprio di quei giocatori a cui facevamo riferimento prima, che hanno avuto questi lievi infortuni muscolari, erano quelli che ci avrebbero un po' dovuto far fare un salto, cercando di proporre un gioco un po' più bello rispetto agli altri anni. Però poi proprio con l'infortunio di Ilić, che era stato un po' preso come direttore d'orchestra, dello stesso Berisha - un ragazzo molto tecnico che sta facendo fatica a rientrare - ci hanno un po' condizionato in questo progetto di proporre magari anche un po' più di possesso palla. E quindi bene o male abbiamo dovuto fare di necessità virtù.

Industry observers note that significa che a gennaio farete qualcosa? "Il mio principale obiettivo è recuperare gli infortunati; i migliori acquisti per me sono gli infortunati che abbiamo in questo momento".

It has been revealed that un retroscena: è vero che il Milan ha chiesto Tiago Gabriel e può confermare che resterà a Lecce almeno fino a fine stagione? "Devo dire, c'è stata giusto una chiacchierata nell'ultimo giorno di mercato, ma quando si tratta di operazioni così grosse, così importanti come quella di Tiago Gabriel, non c'è nemmeno il tempo materiale di impostare una trattativa l'ultimo giorno di mercato. Anche perché poi il mercato è molto lungo, quindi il fatto di iniziare a parlare l'ultimo giorno di mercato tutto sommato significa forse non essere realmente interessati all'operazione, o magari esserlo per un mercato successivo, futuro".

It has been revealed that chiosa poi Cruciani: "A volte c'è bisogno di fare un gioco all'italiana, lo dico in maniera molto semplice: non è uno scandalo giocare alla vecchia maniera. Una bella barricata e ripartire. Farsi prendere in infilata dal Belgio si può evitare, poi magari perdi lo stesso".

" [...] La grande svolta probabilmente arriverà da Cardinale che s’è messo in testa di vincere lo scudetto, quindi ha pronti gli acquisti per sistemare i punti deboli del Milan. Il budget c’è, il nuovo capo dell’area tecnica pure. Come sappiamo, anche se arriverà ufficialmente solo a gennaio, è già operativo il tedesco Markus Krosche, 46 anni, ex Eintracht Francoforte. Per gennaio gli obiettivi sono tre, un centravanti dal gol facile, un difensore centrale e un esterno destro di difesa. Può arrivare Tresoldi? Sarebbe un grande colpo per il Milan, ma anche in chiave nazionale. Il ragazzo, 22 anni, ha sempre tifato i rossoneri. Venire in Italia potrebbe anche convincerlo a scegliere la nazionale azzurra come auspicato da Mancini. Il problema, ovviamente, è il Brugge. La squadra belga chiede una cifra attorno ai sessanta milioni e c’è da verificare la possibilità di trattare già per il mese di gennaio. Su tutto questo stanno lavorando Cardinale e Krosche tenendo aperta anche la porta con il Real Madrid per il brasiliano Endrick, 20 anni.In questo caso sarebbe una operazione diversa, un prestito con qualche clausola. Il problema è Mourinho che non vuole mai mollare i giocatori anche se li utilizza pochissimo come Endrick. Il ragazzino preme, l’anno scorso a gennaio era stato prestato e vorrebbe una soluzione analoga. In corsa c’è pure la Roma, ma Cardinale da tempo ha aperto un canale con Florentino Perez".

  • Manchester United have confirmed that Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become their newly introduced head coach on a two-and-a-half-year contract at Old Trafford.
  • Pochettino will replace Michael Carrick who was sacked following 10 months in charge on Friday, after United agreed to pay more than £10million to buy him and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:02 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 07:51 EST, 13 November 2026.

Manchester United have confirmed that Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become their newly introduced head coach on a two-and-a-half-year contract at Old Trafford.

Pochettino will replace Michael Carrick who was sacked following 10 months in charge on Friday, after United agreed to pay more than £10million to buy him and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

It has been revealed that the 54-year-old Argentine will take charge of the USA’s CONCACAF Nations League double-header against Haiti in Miami on Saturday and Cincinnati on Wednesday before beginning his fresh job as United boss on Wednesday. His first game will be against Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

There were no comments from Pochettino or United officials in Friday’s press release confirming his appointment because he remains contracted to US Soccer.

Pochettino remarked in the USMNT's statement: 'The opportunity to represent the USA crest was one of the greatest honors of my career. We are so grateful to the players for their commitment, to the fans for their belief, and to the Federation for always supporting our staff and creating the opportunities to impact the culture of soccer in this great country.'.

Pochettino is due to give a pre-match press conference at 2.15pm on Friday, but is not expected to speak about United until he arrives next week.

United sources say that Pochettino’s experience, philosophy, personality and skill-set make him well suited for the job, as well as his record of developing individual talent and building excellent team cultures.

Mauricio Pochettino has been appointed as the Manchester United manager.

Michael Carrick was sacked after the club made their worst start to the season in 40 years.

A statement from the club read: ‘Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the Manchester United men’s head coach from 18 November.

‘The club has reached an agreement with the US Soccer Federation for Mauricio and his staff to be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the US men’s national team.

‘The Argentinian is renowned for his high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players.

Industry observers note that ‘Pochettino has consistently performed at the highest level of football across multiple leagues. He began his coaching career with Espanyol in 2009 before joining Southampton and achieving a club-record Premier League points tally in 2014.

‘During five full seasons at Tottenham Hotspur, Pochettino established the club as regular UEFA Champions League contenders, securing qualification in four consecutive seasons and leading the club to its first final in the competition in 2019.

According to recent reports, ‘In 2021, he joined Paris Saint-Germain, where he won the Ligue 1 title, the Coupe de France and the Trophée des Champions before joining Chelsea in 2023. Most recently he led the U.S. Men’s National Team to the Round of 16 at the FIFA World Cup.’.

Earlier in the week, the club's chief executive Omar Berrada and Wilcox flew back from Monaco, where minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe ratified their decision to sack Carrick with the blessing of co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer.

Carrick arrived at United's training ground at 7.50am on Thursday morning and was dismissed.

It has been revealed that he left at 10.18am, less than two and a half hours later. He became the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season.

United's statement read: 'After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

According to recent reports, 'Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club.

'His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.'.

Sources close to United say the club's leadership believe their squad of players is far better than the performances and results under Carrick indicated.

United feel that the squad are far better than their position in the Premier League shows.

They gave the under-fire manager a chance to turn things around against Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa but ultimately felt the team were not on the right path.

It has been a campaign in which United won just three matches, one of which came against Azerbaijani minnows FK Sabah, and they are yet to keep a clean sheet in the league.

Pochettino's United travel to Anfield on November 22 before a Champions League clash at Sporting Lisbon, Pochettino's first home game against Brentford and then away match at Newcastle.

Ma come nasce l'esultanza di Pio Esposito con i muscoli? Interessante aneddoto svelato da Sky Sport sul centravanti dell'Inter, anche ieri a segno nel ko per 4-1 dell'Italia contro il Belgio.

La foto postata dall'Inter sul suo profilo Instagram.

"Una crescita impetuosa, ma non immediata. Dopo gli anni nelle giovanili dell'Inter, Esposito viene ceduto in prestito allo Spezia nell'estate 2023. Il suo primo anno tra i professionisti non è stato semplice: appena 3 gol in 39 presenze in Serie B. Gli allenatori però si fidano di lui, gli danno spazio sia Massimiliano Alvini, attuale tecnico del sorprendente Frosinone, che il subentrante Luca D'Angelo.

In a recent development, esposito vede ancora poco la porta, ma lavora molto: "Ho avuto una crescita fisica importante nell'anno in cui sono andato a La Spezia", ha raccontato a riguardo. "Andavo spesso in palestra con capitan Hristov e quando avevamo finito ci mettevamo in posa allo specchio per vedere i progressi e ci scherzavamo su".

Quando arriva l'ultima giornata di campionato, lo Spezia deve vincere per forza per evitare i playout. L'avversario, il Venezia, si sta giocando la promozione diretta in Serie A e passa in vantaggio. Lo Spezia rimonta e vince 2-1, il pareggio lo segna proprio Esposito. Per esultare gonfia e mostra i bicipiti, come fa con Hristov in palestra davanti allo specchio: "In quella partita ho provato l'esultanza con i muscoli per la prima volta. Mi è piaciuta, è andata bene e ho continuato a riproporla". Nella stagione successiva il boom personale con 19 reti e la promozione in A sfiorata", si legge.

Che emozione è stato il primo gol in Serie A alla Fiorentina? "Il primo gol è sempre una grandissima emozione, al di là di come viene e contro quale squadra. Mi porterò dietro questo gol, mi stimola a lavorare sempre di più e a fare sempre meglio. Continuo a lavorare e spero che ne arrivino altri".

Industry observers note that cosa vi aspettate dal campionato? "Non sai mai cosa aspettarti. Sicuramente incontriamo squadre e giocatori più forti. Non mi aspettavo sicuramente questo inizio di campionato perché c'erano tanti ragazzi nuovi che dovevano adattarsi al gioco del mister, ma l'hanno fatto bene".

According to recent reports, cos'ha di speciale Alvini? "Secondo me la persona. E la personalità. Sono un qualcosa di fantastico. Ci spinge sempre a migliorare e a dare tutto. Questo in allenamento si vede e fa piacere a tutti".

Presto per pensare a qualcosa in più rispetto alla salvezza? "Secondo me la quota salvezza potrebbe essere anche più alta di 40 punti. Speriamo di raggiungerli il prima possibile. Non dobbiamo porci limite, puntiamo sempre più in alto e lavoriamo per farlo".

Industry observers note that che emozioni ti suscita la partita col Milan con entrambe le squadre in alta classifica? "Sicuramente è una squadra importante come le altre che abbiamo affrontare. A San Siro è bellissimo giocare. Però prepariamo questa partita come tutte le altre, andremo a giocarcela a viso aperto".

A chi ti ispiri? "Il mio idolo è sempre stato Sergio Ramos, anche perché nelle giovanili facevo spesso il centrale. E' una passione che è nata dal nulla, lo vedevo giocare e prendevo ispirazione. Ancora oggi guardo suoi vecchi video su Youtube".

It has been revealed that hai il sogno Nazionale? "Sì, come tutti i ragazzi. E' un obiettivo, me lo sono posto, ma senza rincorrerlo con troppa ansia. Punto a lavorare, a far bene, partita dopo partita. Poi se arrivasse la chiamata sarei la persona più felice del mondo".

Parlando della chance del compagno, il danese ne sottolinea l'umiltà e la volontà di imparare anche senza giocare.

In a recent development, dal ritiro della Danimarca, l’esterno della Lazio Gustav Isaksen ha parlato del connazionale e compagno di club Oliver Provstgaard. Ha elogiato le sue prestazioni, collegandole all’impegno mostrato fin dall’arrivo alla Lazio, e ha raccontato come i due si siano aiutati anche fuori dal campo.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Industry observers note that isaksen ha espresso il suo giudizio sul compagno «Provstgaard? Si merita tutto. Dal primo giorno alla Lazio...». Ha quindi ricordato le abitudini di Provstgaard alla Lazio, dove la sua dedizione era evidente già prima delle prestazioni che ora vengono notate: «Provstgaard? È vero che sta offrendo prestazioni ottime, ma dal primo giorno alla Lazio è stato il primo ad arrivare e l'ultimo ad andare, si è fatto in quattro.».

According to recent reports, il rendimento di Provstgaard ha colto di sorpresa chi non conosceva né lui né il Vejle. Isaksen ha descritto così quella reazione: «La gente è rimasta sorpresa, nessuno lo conosceva lui né il Vejle.».

According to recent reports, per l’esterno, in certi contesti il percorso precedente pesa meno di quanto un giocatore riesce a mostrare una volta arrivato: «In certi contesti non conta tanto ciò che hai fatto in passato, ma solo quello che dimostri in allenamento». Nelle sue parole conta anche il tipo di persona che si dimostra di essere.

It has been revealed that secondo Isaksen, Provstgaard ha compreso subito questo aspetto. Il modo in cui si è presentato alla Lazio ha mostrato sia la volontà di farne parte sia le qualità per continuare a giocare nel club: «Lui l'ha capito bene e fin da subito ha dimostrato di voler essere qui e di avere le qualità necessarie per restarci.».

Isaksen ha poi ripercorso il periodo in cui il compagno non giocava e il momento in cui ha avuto la sua opportunità, sottolineando l’atteggiamento mantenuto nel frattempo: «È stato umile e consapevole che, anche senza giocare, avrebbe potuto imparare dagli altri. E poi, quasi senza accorgersene, è arrivata la sua chance, perché se l'è guadagnata.».

#2738. England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation

📅 26 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 32m • 📚 Deep Dive (6433 w)

England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation

📅 26 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 32 min read (6433 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~32 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that there had been so much talk – first raised by Thomas Tuchel after the shocking World Cup exit to Argentina – about England’s DNA.
  • It has been revealed that the world and European champions were England’s first opponents – after the World Cup – in this Nations League campaign and came away from Wembley with a deserved win.
  • Sources indicate that mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there had been so much talk – first raised by Thomas Tuchel after the shocking World Cup exit to Argentina – about England’s DNA. About whether they could keep the ball, pass the ball, control the ball, the way Spain do.

It has been revealed that the world and European champions were England’s first opponents – after the World Cup – in this Nations League campaign and came away from Wembley with a deserved win. They are now 39 games unbeaten with substitute Mikel Oyarzabal, who scored the winning goal against England in the final of the last European Championship, doing so again.

Sources indicate that mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN! 🎯Spain retake the lead after a slick finish from the Spaniard 👏#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pPT3KvRHWl.

Industry observers note that that may have been no surprise, even if the inevitable “olés” after Spain’s third goal will have hurt. But the nature of it? For the England manager this was another shocker. Not in the way his team went about the task. They were positive, fun, attacking. But in the way they conceded – goals and chances – and lost.

On this performance, DNA, for England, stands for Defensively Not Able, as they threw away what could have been a famous and restorative victory. Instead, with Croatia beating the Czech Republic in the other group game, England are under immediate pressure to win in Prague on Tuesday.

In fact, England have conceded 13 goals in their past six matches – in fairness including four in that third-place World Cup 6-4 win over France – and that is not good enough for a top-tier nation. Tuchel needs to sort it out defensively.

It could have been very different if Harry Kane had not missed from the penalty spot, slipping as he struck the ball, with England improbably 2-1 ahead. “It would have been the decisive punch,” Tuchel stated. Maybe so, even if there was always the feeling that Spain could go through the gears.

According to recent reports, kane MISSES from the penalty spot! 😧Harry Kane slips when he strikes the ball, let off for Spain and Luis de la Fuente#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pvg3GGa9ma.

Afterwards there were claims, led by the impressive Anthony Gordon, that this was a missed opportunity for England. A bit like the World Cup. They need to shake this theme.

Industry observers note that the irony was this was one of their best creative displays for quite some time. They took the game to Spain and could have scored more. And conceded more.

In truth it could have been Spain 4 England 0 inside half an hour and before Tuchel’s team laid a glove on their opponents.

Another let off for England 😧Ferran Torres misses another significant chance one-on-one with James Trafford #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/KFkJoJUW6c.

The manager had also spoken about how England should “embrace the chaos” as their best route to success. That may appear a questionable tactic – does chaos ever win a tournament? – but England certainly did that. This was as chaotic and, admittedly, entertaining as it gets.

England attacked with pace and power with the pick of their players the two based in Spain: Gordon, who scored, and Jude Bellingham. And the defenders? This was a bad night for Marc Guéhi, his Manchester City team-mate Nico O’Reilly (cue speculation about whether they were distracted by the verdict on the Premier League charges against their club) and for Jarell Quansah at right-back who is so evidently a centre-half.

A penny, once more, for the thoughts of the unused Trent Alexander-Arnold. The fourth defender, Ezri Konsa, vented his frustration at what was happening around him.

In a recent development, it was not just the errors but the unforced nature of them. Poor in possession with misplaced passes and defensively wide open. There is a gap between Spain and England but not as big as the gaps that were exposed in England’s back four. They endured a full house of calamities. They seemed strangely unaware – or incapable of dealing with – the danger posed by the outstanding Lamine Yamal.

In a recent development, maybe because of the opposition – or the criticism – England felt the need to play out. But what an horrific start. What an inexplicable moment for Guéhi as he received the ball from O’Reilly and turned into trouble, gifting possession to Yamal who ran on and scored. Inside two minutes.

WHAT A START FROM SPAIN 🇪🇸Lamine Yamal pounces on a Marc Guéhi error to give Spain an early lead at Wembley #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/Et83EyTPlp.

Recent findings suggest that spain walked out with the second star on their shirt – to mark their second World Cup triumph. That was the star Tuchel had promised for England.

It has been revealed that now, straight away, they were up against it. It could have turned very ugly. Ferran Torres, who had scored the winner in the World Cup Final, had one disallowed for offside, then was thwarted by James Trafford after – inexplicably again – being played onside by Quansah.

MAJOR SAVE from James Trafford 🧤The Leeds United goalkeeper keeps out Ferran Torres#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/nj5b8AUSQU.

Then Torres was sent clear following Elliot Anderson’s poor pass, only to drag his shot wide. The third miss came from Dani Olmo, again set up by Yamal.

It could – it should – have been game over. Then England unexpectedly turned it around. They had kept attacking despite what was going on at the back and struck through a truly thrilling counter-attack, with Gordon and Bellingham combining before the Barcelona winger calmly beat goalkeeper Unai Simon.

ENGLAND ARE LEVEL! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿A brilliant finish from Anthony Gordon after a breathtaking counter attack 👏#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/z0nSfWIHVd.

It was an exceptional goal and was quickly followed by a fortunate one as O’Reilly’s cross was met by Kane who stooped to steer in a header, only for it to strike Marc Cucurella, who made a mess of clearing, and it went past Simón.

I think we'll give that goal to Harry Kane 🎯England come from behind to lead Spain thanks Harry Kane, with assistance from Marc Cucurella ⚽️#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/X3qSOWUhVT.

The Spain left-back hit the post with a cross, misjudged by Trafford who was given this game and the next to stake his claim ahead of Jordan Pickford who has so long been the undisputed first-choice.

England dominated for a while and Bellingham won a penalty, after a VAR intervention, only for Kane to strike the crossbar.

Industry observers note that how Spain made them pay and worryingly so. O’Reilly passed the ball straight to Olmo who swept it inside. Substitute Álex Baena checked and beat Trafford from the edge of the area. Even worse was how Spain cut through the heart of England defence with Baena finding Oyarzabal. Why was no defender closer to him? What was Guéhi doing? And O’Reilly? Oyarzabal exquisitely dinked the ball over Trafford.

Thomas Tuchel does not think Manchester City’s guilty verdict over almost all of their Premier League charges distracted his England players in the Nations League defeat to Spain.

City players Marc Guéhi and Nico O’Reilly were at fault for two of Spain’s goals and both Tuchel, the head coach, and England captain Harry Kane confirmed news of the verdict had been discussed among the squad.

Tuchel does not plan to address the glitch with his players ahead of the remaining Nations League games against Czech Republic and Croatia.

Recent findings suggest that asked if the City verdict had been a cause of discussion ahead of the Spain game, Tuchel replied: “Not for me, but I can imagine maybe for the Man City players. I won’t comment on it as it’s an ongoing case.

Sources indicate that “I didn’t make it a topic. It was not a topic for me. I’m just thinking about Spain and the team and meetings. The players have more time than me. So I can imagine they talk about it. It’s good they do. I don’t think it was a distraction for them.”.

Kane added: “There was a discussion, but when we’re with England, we kind of put club football to one side and it was no different this week.”.

Tuchel also refused to point the finger of blame at Guéhi, O’Reilly or Kane, who missed a penalty, for England’s defeat despite admitting his team got off to the worst possible start by conceding a goal after two minutes.

“We will focus on the positives, but also highlight the stuff we can do better,” Tuchel mentioned. “Not even speaking about individual mistakes because this is normal. It just happens. It should not happen, and for sure not in this amount. But there is no sense in showing the individual mistakes or telling them ‘please don’t make mistakes’. That is normal, but we can do things better. We can defend the third goal better. But we will focus on the positives. There is a lot to take away from the game.

“We wanted to be the team desperately to beat them [Spain] and we think we had them. We still think we had them at half-time. That was the way the team demonstrated up after half-time. So we will focus on that, but the reality is we lost and the reality is we need to prove it again.”.

“It was a terrible start, the worst possible start, which makes it so difficult against a team like this. The reaction was very good. After 10/12 minutes, we were the better team but we gave away too many mistakes. We were the better team. If we had converted the penalty, it could have been the decisive moment. We have to keep going and learn from the mistakes. We could have created more if we had been more clinical in the final 20 metres. We showed great bravery and courage with our high-ball wins. There will always be moments you suffer against teams like this. The effort and quality were there tonight but the result does not prove it today.”.

According to recent reports, “I think there is a gap [between Spain and England]. They [Spain] are the world champions and European champions. Mikel Oyarzabal was never going to miss. He was always in control of the situation. Honestly, people talk about sexy football, that is sexy football. I would watch that all night.”.

🗣️ "We went toe to toe with the European and world champions" 💪Harry Kane remains positive about England performance despite their 3-2 defeat to Spain 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿🇪🇸#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @England pic.twitter.com/qkhqsqmPEl.

🗣️ "You have to beat them to show people we can do this" 💪@IanWright0 reflects on England's 3-2 defeat to Spain at Wembley#ITVFootball | @markpougatch pic.twitter.com/ko2FYs4VqA.

In a recent development, marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly may want to look away now but Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon scored well. Our very own Mike McGrath has provided his player ratings.

Tonight: England 2 Spain 3 (H)Tuesday September 29: Czech Republic (A), kick-off 7.45pmSaturday October 3: Croatia (A), kick-off 5pmTuesday October 6: Czech Republic (H), kick-off 7.45pm.

🗣️ "I think it's a bit of a missed chance" 👀Anthony Gordon says mistakes cost England the win tonight against Spain at Wembley 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @England pic.twitter.com/AJBxVNjbjq.

Sources indicate that A highly entertaining game. England will probably argue the game changed on Kane’s missed penalty, but Spain missed a lot of very clear chances and will feel they deserved the victory. A losing start to the Nations League for Tuchel and his team, but there were some positives. Gordon, Bellingham and Anderson were all excellent. Some of the defending, not so excellent.

Possession: England 47%-53% SpainShots: 13-15Shots on target: 5-5Corners: 6-3Touches in opposition box: 37-15.

England have one last chance with a corner out on the left. This will be it. Spain are able to deal with it and clear their lines.

Then comes the final whistle at Wembley and the world champions Spain claim a 3-2 victory in north London. It was an absorbing game, where momentum swung one way and then the other, but it is Spain who are the victors.

Baena brings down Rogers with a silly challenge to gift England a free-kick deep in the Spanish half. This could be England’s last chance.

Anderson is over it but his delivery is poor, easily caught by Unai Simon.

England are running out of time to find an equaliser.

O’Reilly appears to be suffering with cramp but England have made all five substitutions.

There will be five added minutes.

A late change for England as Branthwaite replaces Guehi.

Rogers delivers a dangerous cross from the right that runs through the six-yard box and forces Pubill to put it behind for a corner.

England take it short before Anderson clips it in but Laporte heads away.

In a recent development, garner should have done so much better with that. His run into the Spain box on the left side is picked out by Anderson’s pass. Garner has Calvert-Lewin waiting at the back post but the former massively overhits the cross.

It has been revealed that double substitution from England as Calvert-Lewin and Gibbs-White replace Kane and Saka. Rare to say Kane taken off, especially when England are behind.

Recent findings suggest that saka goes down under a challenge from Cucurella inside the Spain penalty box but no penalty is forthcoming. VAR has cleared the incident. Moments later, Bellingham is then booked for stopping Spain going on the counter.

Spain make a change as Merino replaces Olmo.

It has been revealed that the way Spain control possession and keep the ball is impressive. They toy with you pretty well and often look so composed.

Baena, who has been superb since coming on, feeds a lovely pass into the path of Oyarzabal on the right side of the box. Oyarzabal takes one touch before lifting it over Trafford into the England net. That is a lovely assist from Baena and lovely finish from Oyarzabal.

Mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN! 🎯Spain retake the lead after a slick finish from the Spaniard 👏#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pPT3KvRHWl.

Industry observers note that given the quality of the opposition and the sustained threat he carried, that might have been Gordon’s best-ever performance in an England shirt. Him and Bellingham have been excellent. But now he’s been replaced by Morgan Rogers.

It has been revealed that guehi joins O’Reilly in the book for a cynical foul on Olmo. You can put that yellow card in the category of a professional foul.

England are making a double change as Garner and Rogers come on for Lewis-Skelly and Gordon. Garner was not in the initial squad but takes his chance now after the withdrawals.

Spain also make a substitution as Pedri replaces Ruiz.

At one end, Yamal has a shot blocked after England gave the ball away before Lewis-Skelly’s shot down the other end is easily saved.

The first booking of the night sees O’Reilly shown a yellow card for a foul on Yamal.

England come close to going back in front. After good work from Bellingham, Saka has it on the right side of the box. Saka cuts inside onto his left and looks to pick out the far corner but his effort goes narrowly wide.

Another big mistake from England is punished. It is absolutely dreadful from O’Reilly, who gives the ball away so poorly deep inside the England half. Spain capitalise and it is the man who has only just come on, Baena, who curls into the bottom corner from the edge of the box. All to play for with half an hour to go at Wembley.

Recent findings suggest that SPAIN EQUALISE! 🇪🇸A brilliant finish from Alex Baena after a Nico O'Reilly mistake 🎯#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/tXygPfbPmb.

Yamal and Baena exchange a lovely one-two on the right side of the box and you think the former will find the far corner but his effort goes wide.

In a recent development, how did Yamal MISS that! 🤯A massive opportunity goes begging to pull Spain level! #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/jyzLm9VBd5.

Industry observers note that cucurella has a real habit of making himself unpopular wherever he plays. The Wembley crowd have been booing his every touch and were not happy with him staying down after the ball hit him in the head. Spain haven’t got going at all in this second half.

Spain have made a double change as Oyarzabal and Baena replace Torres and Williams.

Kane steps up but his effort smashes into the bar. Kane slipped just as he took it. In fact, a free-kick is given to Spain as it was a double hit.

Sources indicate that kane MISSES from the penalty spot! 😧Harry Kane slips when he strikes the ball, let off for Spain and Luis de la Fuente#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pvg3GGa9ma.

According to recent reports, the referee overturns the original decision and points to the spot. A foul from a Barcelona midfielder on a Real Madrid midfielder is given.

Yet more England appeals for a penalty. Bellingham goes down, believing he was fouled by Rodri, but the referee gives nothing. There is contact but is it enough for a penalty? The referee had a good view and there is a decent shout for a penalty.

The referee is being sent to the screen so we know what that usually means...

Sources indicate that certainly no sitting on the lead from England at the start of the second half. Tuchel was adamant that Bellingham should have been awarded a penalty after going down in the area.

And Tuchel might get his way as VAR have sent referee Davide Massa to the screen.

England want a penalty. Saka goes down under a challenge from Laporte from behind but those appeals are waved away. VAR checks and clears the incident. Laporte got the ball.

Sources indicate that chance for England. Bellingham’s cross from the left picks out Quansah in the centre of the box but the defender’s header from eight yards out misses the target. What an opportunity that was for Quansah to score his first international goal.

It has been revealed that spain are unbeaten in nearly 40 competitive matches and, as it stands, that run is set to come to an end. Still a long way to come though tonight and Spain could have been 3-0 up before England even scored one goal.

We are back under way at Wembley. No changes for either side at the break.

Harry Kane wants England to address how they lost their identity and went “against our beliefs” at the World Cup.

In a brutally honest assessment of the tournament, the England captain admitted Thomas Tuchel’s team did not play to their full potential in several games – even before the painful semi-final exit against Argentina.

Kane, who played golf instead of watching the World Cup final, revealed the 2-1 Atlanta defeat hurt more than missing a penalty four years earlier in Qatar, when England were knocked out by France in the quarter-finals.

“This one hurt more than any other one. I would probably say even more than when I missed a penalty in Qatar because of the manner that it happened,” Kane stated. “It was not us as a team.

According to recent reports, “We trust our players and the player know very well that if you miss a camp then someone plays well in your position that the competition is always on. You have to make sure to be available and to produce top-level performances in camp and if you do so, that counts for something. Right now, it is not on my list of worries. I am not wired like this. From the moment I arrived at SGP my full focus is 100 per cent with the players who are here.

“There is no threat, distrust or threat of consequences. It will come naturally. I truly believe that we have the opposite. You will talk to our captain, Harry Kane, who has the most minutes for club and country and is happy to be here while teammates of his are enjoying a 10-day break. He is the role model and that is the vibe we have here.”.

They do have plenty to cheer about:.

James Trafford is poised to start for England ahead of Jordan Pickford against Spain tonight.

Pickford has been England’s No1 for eight years but Thomas Tuchel is set to make a change to face the world champions in the Nations League opener at Wembley.

Trafford went to the World Cup in the summer and has started the Premier League in good form following his move to Leeds.

In the first match since the World Cup, changing his goalkeeper is a major selection decision from Tuchel.

Elsewhere, Jarell Quansah is set to play at right-back ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold while Myles Lewis-Skelly is also in line to return to the starting XI after being recalled into the squad after missing the World Cup.

England begin their Nations League campaign with a home game against the world champions Spain. This is England’s first game since the World Cup, with their dreams of glory ended by Argentina in the semi-finals, but they did finish third after beating France in a high-scoring third/fourth play-off. The last meeting between these sides saw Spain beat England to win Euro 2024. They also faced off in the Nations League back in 2018, with Spain winning at Wembley and England taking victory over in Spain.

Industry observers note that england’s looks for these games has been disrupted by a number of withdrawals. Cole Palmer had earned a recall having been left out of the World Cup squad but the Chelsea forward has withdrawn due to a minor injury, despite playing the full game for Chelsea against Brentford in the final game before the international beak.

According to recent reports, “He [Palmer] plays with discomfort and pain and cannot play on the highest level with discomfort and pain,” Tuchel remarked. “Chelsea informed us. That is my understanding. We are not managing load. This is not an ‘international break’. It is a competitive environment, where the players love to train and be together. That is what we created. We will never compromise on that. We will never let this feeling creep in that the players do not want to come [to England camps]. We focus on the guys who absolutely want to play for England.

“For sure it is a missed opportunity. It is another missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities. I do not blame him for it, it is just a fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries. I only want to rely on what I personally witness and see within my team. For that you have to be in camp. If you are not in camp there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve because you can only do it with me on the pitch and with us on the pitch. It is a missed opportunity.”.

In a recent development, declan Rice has also withdrawn from the squad despite playing the full game in Arsenal’s defeat to Brighton as have Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento. Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner have been called up as a result.

Sources indicate that trent Alexander-Arnold is back in the fold for the first time since June 2025. 18-year-old Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha made his England debut against Upcoming Zealand during the World Cup warm-ups and takes his place in this squad, although he does make the matchday squad for tonight’s game. England will also take on Czechia, Croatia and then Cezchia again during this international break.

According to recent reports, having been crowned world champions back in July, Spain are now champions of both Europe and the world. Back in June 2025, Spain made the Nations League final but lost on penalties to Portugal. Ahead of this international window, The Royal Spanish Federation has extended Luis de la Fuente’s contract until 2032. After tonight, Spain will host Croatia and Czechia before travelling to Croatia to cap off this international window.

This is an extended international break, with four games to take place during this window. Team news from Wembley to follow shortly.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that "Abbiamo un gruppo solido, con elementi prestati anche alla Nazionale maggiore.
  • Baldini dà grande valore anche ai pareggi, soprattutto per l'atteggiamento mostrato dalla squadra: "Questi risultati sono come vittorie per lo spirito che abbiamo dimostrato.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that un pareggio che vale molto più di un semplice punto. Silvio Baldini, commissario tecnico dell'Italia Under 21, promuove la prestazione dei suoi ragazzi dopo il 2-2 contro il Belgio a Livorno. Il selezionatore ha sottolineato soprattutto lo spirito di una squadra che non ha paura di rischiare, che sa soffrire e che considera ogni partita un'occasione per crescere. Un gruppo solido, composto anche da elementi che rappresentano il futuro della Nazionale maggiore e che hanno già attirato l'attenzione di Mancini.

It has been revealed that "Abbiamo un gruppo solido, con elementi prestati anche alla Nazionale maggiore. Adesso aspettiamo marzo, quando avremo altre due amichevoli per ritrovarci, giocare insieme e permettere ai ragazzi di cercare un feeling sempre maggiore. Siamo una famiglia: chiunque entra si mette a disposizione e riesce a offrire ottime prestazioni. Il nostro motto è 'morire ma non mollare'".

Baldini dà grande valore anche ai pareggi, soprattutto per l'atteggiamento mostrato dalla squadra: "Questi risultati sono come vittorie per lo spirito che abbiamo dimostrato. Non abbiamo avuto paura di perdere. Avremmo potuto dire di stare tranquilli e ragionare, invece ci abbiamo provato, mettendoci il cuore per capire fin dove potevamo arrivare. Ci sono anche delle cicatrici, qualcuno voleva trasformare ogni episodio in una rissa: bisogna soltanto giocare a calcio".

Il commissario tecnico guarda poi al rapporto tra Under 21 e Nazionale maggiore, sottolineando come la crescita dei giovani debba essere un obiettivo comune: "Lavoriamo per questo, per la Nazionale maggiore. Dispiace per la sconfitta degli Azzurri, ma ieri tutti i miei ragazzi hanno fatto il tifo per loro. Il calcio è anche questo: bisogna accettare le sconfitte, perché nel percorso ci sono difficoltà. Per crescere non bisogna cercare scuse, ma essere bravi".

It has been revealed that sulla gestione degli ultimi minuti, quando l'Italia ha trovato il gol del pareggio a quattro minuti dalla fine, Baldini spiega le difficoltà incontrate contro la costruzione belga: "Il problema era che non riuscivamo a portare una pressione ordinata sulla loro linea difensiva. Loro erano bravi a coinvolgere il portiere e a cercare i lanci lunghi verso i due attaccanti. Dovevamo andare in pressione prima, ma non sempre ci riuscivamo e il portiere riusciva a mettere palloni pericolosi". Infine, una battuta sul possibile legame con Livorno e sulla possibilità di allenare in futuro in una piazza del genere: "Nella vita possono esserci delle opportunità, ma queste non sono piazze facili. Quando decidi di allenare qui devi sapere di essere sostenuto in tutto, perché se i risultati non arrivano rischi di essere lasciato solo. Conoscendo il vento, cerco di fare le mie valutazioni: quando c'è il libeccio, in mare è meglio non andare".
