📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il vicepresidente dell'Inter e leggenda del club nerazzurro, Javier Zanetti, ha parlato a margine del "Premio Modello Virtuoso del Calcio Italiano", intitolato a Italo Galbiati. Ecco le sue parole raccolte da TuttoMercatoWeb.com: "Il significato di questa serata, di questo premio? Sono onorato e orgoglioso di prendere questo premio in memoria di Italo Galbiati, ringrazio tutte le persone che hanno pensato a me per questo premio".

It has been revealed that L'Inter si conferma sempre, oggi un altro oro da aggiungere ai trofei dell'anno scorso, la Panchina d'Oro di Chivu. "Sono felicissimo per Cristian perché merita questa Panchina d'Oro, per quello che sta facendo, quello che ha fatto e quello che farà. Conosco Cristian da quando eravamo compagni, è un fratello per me e sinceramente non avevo dubbi su tutto quello che lui poteva fare. E credo che stia facendo, insieme a tutti noi, assieme a una squadra di ragazzi con grande personalità e grande responsabilità, un ottimo lavoro".

In a recent development, quanto è cresciuto Chivu in questi anni? "Mi è piaciuto tantissimo perché ha fatto un percorso con noi nel settore giovanile. Lì si vedeva la sua visione, la sua ambizione e la sua passione per questo sport. Da quando è con noi in prima squadra, noi non avevamo dubbi perché è uno di famiglia. Sa trasmettere i valori che noi vogliamo per i nostri giocatori e conosce i valori che ha l'Inter. Allora per questo credo che lui in certi momenti sa fare la differenza".

According to recent reports, chivu non si è mai nascosto, ha detto: "Partiamo per vincere tutto". "Non ci siamo mai nascosti noi come società. Siamo una società, un gruppo di giocatori che quando si sbaglia non cerchiamo alibi, ci prendiamo le nostre responsabilità, cerchiamo sempre di guardare avanti e credo che questo sia una cosa molto importante per un gruppo e una società che è ambiziosa e che vuole competere per grandi traguardi".

Questo vuol dire che dopo il double dello scorso anno si deve aggiungere qualcosa e si deve puntare anche fuori dai nostri confini, per la Champions? "No, questo vuol dire che vogliamo essere competitivi in tutte le competizioni che dovremo giocare. E credo che ci siano i presupposti per poter far bene e per poter sperare. Non è semplice, non sarà facile perché sono tre competizioni difficilissime. Già il campionato italiano è molto equilibrato, stiamo vedendo che tutte le squadre sono lì a pochi punti e sarà da lottare fino alla fine".

It has been revealed that il tuo ruolo è stato fondamentale in quell'operazione: quanto sei orgoglioso di Lautaro Martínez? "Sono felicissimo per Lauti perché quando ci siamo conosciuti, che lui era molto giovane, noi ci aspettavamo questo suo presente. Sinceramente è un ragazzo di grande personalità, che trasmette grande senso di appartenenza, che ha una grandissima voglia sempre di mettersi per primo a disposizione e siamo contenti che sia il nostro capitano".

Sources indicate that E vedere Nico Paz all'Inter rimane un sogno per lei o ci crede ancora? "Nico Paz è un giocatore del Como e io lo rispetto per questo, e sono felicissimo che stia facendo molto bene nella Nazionale argentina".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that stando ai documenti ufficiali, il Napoli ha archiviato l’esercizio al 30 giugno 2026 con un valore della produzione di 384,3 milioni di euro, rispetto ai circa 291 milioni dell’annata precedente.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, chiude con un bilancio utile la SSC Napoli dopo la perdita registrata nell’esercizio precedente. Il ritorno in Champions League, il peso delle operazioni di mercato, il risarcimento ottenuto nell’ambito del contenzioso con IMG e lo sviluppo del comparto commerciale hanno permesso alla società partenopea di migliorare i propri risultati economici, a fronte di una crescita altrettanto significativa dei costi.

Industry observers note that stando ai documenti ufficiali, il Napoli ha archiviato l’esercizio al 30 giugno 2026 con un valore della produzione di 384,3 milioni di euro, rispetto ai circa 291 milioni dell’annata precedente. E’ un primato assoluto nella storia della società di Aurelio De Laurentiis, che supera anche i 359,2 milioni contabilizzati nel 2022/2023, stagione culminata con la conquista del terzo scudetto. Le entrate derivanti dai diritti televisivi hanno raggiunto quota 133 milioni di euro, contro i 78,1 milioni della stagione 2024/2025. Nello specifico, gli introiti provenienti dalle competizioni UEFA sono cresciuti da 3,9 a 49,5 milioni di euro, ai quali si aggiungono quelli legati alla partecipazione alla Supercoppa italiana. Le plusvalenze derivanti dalle cessioni dei calciatori si sono attestate intorno ai 102,7 milioni di euro. L’operazione più remunerativa è stata quella riguardante Victor Osimhen, che ha assicurato al club una plusvalenza di circa 73,2 milioni di euro. Tra le altre cessioni più significative ci sono quelle di Giacomo Raspadori, Alessandro Zanoli e Giovanni Simeone. I trasferimenti a titolo temporaneo hanno inoltre generato proventi per circa 8,7 milioni di euro. Nel dettaglio, ecco come si compongono i ricavi della SSC Napoli: Ricavi da gare: 31,3 milioni di euro (24,1 milioni nel 2024/2025); Ricavi da sponsorizzazioni: 52,9 milioni (48,1 milioni); Ricavi commerciali e royalties: 25,5 milioni (20,1 milioni); Proventi vari: 1,7 milioni (1,3 milioni); Proventi da cessione dei diritti televisivi: 133 milioni (78,1 milioni); Plusvalenze da cessione dei calciatori: 102,7 milioni (102,6 milioni); Altri ricavi e proventi diversi: 36,8 milioni (16,6 milioni); Contributi in conto esercizio: 500mila euro (0 euro); Totale: 384,3 milioni (290,9 milioni). Nella voce relativa agli altri proventi rientra anche un’entrata straordinaria derivante dall’accordo transattivo raggiunto dalla Lega Serie A nell’ambito della controversia con IMG per i diritti audiovisivi internazionali. L’intesa ha garantito alla società azzurra un introito di 19,3 milioni di euro.

Nell’esercizio chiuso al 30 giugno 2022, il Napoli aveva contabilizzato 12,1 milioni di euro di ricavi da gara e ulteriori 37,2 milioni provenienti da sponsorizzazioni, attività commerciali e royalties, per un totale di 49,3 milioni. Nella stagione 2025/2026, queste stesse voci hanno raggiunto complessivamente 109,7 milioni di euro, di cui: 31,3 milioni derivanti dal matchday, 52,9 milioni dalle sponsorizzazioni e 25,5 milioni dalle attività commerciali e dalle royalties.

Aumentano anche i costi di gestione. I costi della produzione hanno raggiunto quota 373,3 milioni di euro, rispetto ai 315,5 milioni dell’esercizio precedente, con una crescita di circa il 18%. Di seguito il dettaglio delle principali voci di costo del bilancio azzurro:.

-Materie prime, sussidiarie, di consumo e merci: 10,4 milioni di euro (6,5 milioni nel 2024/2025);.

-Costi per servizi: 30,5 milioni (36 milioni); Costi per godimento di beni di terzi: 8,1 milioni (6,7 milioni);.

-Costi per il personale: 172,3 milioni (142,1 milioni), di cui 165,3 milioni per salari e stipendi (135,8 milioni);.

-Ammortamenti e svalutazioni: 135 milioni (118,2 milioni);.

-Variazione delle rimanenze: -800mila euro (-100mila euro);.

-Oneri diversi di gestione: 17,7 milioni (6,2 milioni); Totale: 373,3 milioni (315,5 milioni).

Industry observers note that A incidere maggiormente sull’aumento delle spese è stato il costo della squadra, anche in delle virtù operazioni sul mercato effettuate per soddisfare le richieste dell’ex allenatore Antonio Conte. Infatti, la voce salari è cresciuta dai 132,9 milioni dell’esercizio precedente ai 161,9 milioni contabilizzati al 30 giugno 2026. I soli compensi contrattuali dei calciatori hanno raggiunto quota 128,9 milioni di euro, ai quali si aggiungono i premi legati al conseguimento dei risultati sportivi, anch’essi in aumento.

Sources indicate that tuttavia, la crescita del fatturato ha permesso al Napoli di tornare a registrare un risultato economico positivo. La differenza tra il valore ei costi della produzione si è attestata intorno agli 11 milioni di euro, invertendo la tendenza negativa dell’esercizio precedente. Al netto della componente fiscale, il Napoli ha archiviato il bilancio al 30 giugno 2026 con un utile di circa 2,2 milioni di euro. Un risultato in netto miglioramento rispetto alla perdita di 21,4 milioni di euro registrata dodici mesi prima. Il club partenopeo torna quindi in utile dopo un solo anno caratterizzato da un risultato economico negativo, raggiungendo contestualmente il fatturato più elevato della propria storia.

In a recent development, infine, sul documento contabile ci sono indicazioni significative anche sulla situazione patrimoniale e finanziaria della SSC Napoli. Il patrimonio netto si mantiene ampiamente positivo, attestandosi a circa 192,4 milioni di euro, mentre le disponibilità liquide ammontano a 172,9 milioni.

(ANSA) - ROMA, 16 NOV - "Una scelta di buon senso, perché un'ulteriore iniziativa contenziosa avrebbe soltanto alimentato tensioni delle quali il calcio italiano non ha alcun bisogno, senza offrire alcun contributo al confronto sui programmi e sul futuro della Federazione". Giovanni Malagò, in una dichiarazione all'ANSA, accoglie favorevolmente la decisione di Adriano Galliani di non impugnare il provvedimento di ammissione della sua candidatura alla presidenza della federcalcio, evidenziando però che le polemiche in avvicinamento si sarebbero potute evitare. "Già la contestazione relativa alla nomina della Commissione, sollevata senza neppure richiedere un chiarimento che sarebbe stato semplice fornire, ha generato inutili allarmismi in un clima fin troppo teso - spiega -, certamente non per mia iniziativa. Il richiamo alla responsabilità e alla serenità del percorso elettorale è dunque apprezzato e condivisibile.

Recent findings suggest that la coerenza con questi obiettivi si misura, però, anzitutto nella capacità di evitare polemiche ed iniziative pretestuose, non soltanto nella rinuncia a darvi ulteriore seguito". Il commissario straordinario della Figc continuerà "a privilegiare il confronto sui contenuti e il dialogo con tutte le componenti del sistema, nell'interesse del calcio italiano". (ANSA).

Former Old Firm rivals reveal how clubs walked a fine line between rivalry and respect...and even stopped by for tea and sympathy in times of trouble!

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:20 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 12:29 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • They have reached an age when they would once have been categorised as the old infirm.
  • It has been revealed that they have reached the age when they can reflect on being stalwarts of the Old Firm.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:20 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 12:29 EST, 13 November 2026.

They have reached an age when they would once have been categorised as the old infirm. Yet in the autumn of 2026 they cavort around Toryglen with an almost juvenile vigour.

It has been revealed that they have reached the age when they can reflect on being stalwarts of the Old Firm. Yet they are outlining looks and strategy for a vital, growing movement.

Recent findings suggest that the two meetings are separated by two sets of stairs. On the ground level, men of pensionable age and beyond play walking football. Just above sit Campbell Ogilvie, former secretary of Rangers and president of the Scottish FA, and Eric Riley, once company secretary and director of Celtic.

They are both on the board of Walking Football Scotland, an organisation that now has more than 5,000 people playing the game across 160 clubs, with participants ranging from 40 to 93.

The venerable statesmen of the Scottish game may be perceived to be rivals, but only in matters on the pitch. They sit in an office in the south side of Glasgow and reminisce about how they first met 50 years ago when playing five-a-sides and then renewed that rivalry in their professional life.

As the Glasgow rivals now seem regularly at odds, both men recalled a time when friendship was paramount amid the sporting mayhem.

Former Rangers secretary Campbell Ogilvie and ex-Celtic director Eric Riley are firm friends.

It has been revealed that ‘The two clubs always had a good relationship back in those days,’ stated Ogilvie, now 76 and still playing football. ‘We wanted to beat each other — naturally. But off the field we had a very close relationship.’.

He told a remarkable story that backs that assertion.

‘There was one day I was at Ibrox in the early 1980s when the team was not doing so well. The phone rang and it was Sean Fallon, Jock Stein’s former Celtic assistant. I had known Sean from my days with the Scottish League and he said: “I know you’re going through a rocky spell, so I’m coming over for a cup of tea”.

‘Over he comes. So there was a very close relationship in those days. I’m not there now and for all I know there still is. But certainly, when I was there and Eric was at Celtic, we could talk to each other.’.

Riley, 69, agreed: ‘Absolutely. John McClelland (former Rangers chairman) was one we could talk to. And Martin (Bain, former chief executive) I suppose, when he came along a bit later. Between myself and Peter Lawwell (former Celtic chief executive and chairman) the relationship between the clubs off the field was actually quite strong. But on the field we still wanted to win.’.

Ogilvie added: ‘There was a respect. And I go back to the Willie Waddells and the Willie Thorntons, there was that respect. More recently that was there with the likes of Jack McGinn and so on.

Sources indicate that ‘We had a good relationship but it’s fair to say that there was no social media in those days. You know all the toxic stuff that can bring.’.

Sources indicate that the traits of respect and sporting competitiveness have been obvious in both men since they first met half a century ago. ‘We played five-a-side football at Scotstoun before the football careers started. It was just casual games,’ said Ogilvie. ‘We were in our early 20s. Eric was an accountant and I think those games were arranged through accountants.

‘I played youth football when I was 16 and, 60 years down the line, playing football is still a major part of my life.’.

In a recent development, ogilvie began walking football eight years ago and Riley soon after. ‘I suffer from Parkinson’s, amongst other things,’ said Riley. ‘I was getting assistance through Stobhill Hospital and the physiotherapist there, who specialises in Parkinson’s patients, got in touch to say there was a project going on at Toryglen where they were playing walking football and assessing you to see what the benefits may or may not be.’.

Ogilvie and Riley are both on the board of Walking Football and have played a substantial role in its rise.

Recent findings suggest that riley agreed to take part. ‘I really enjoyed it because you are back playing football again, you have the camaraderie and you have the home baking which I never really get at home.’.

Riley had a hip replacement in March and admitted: ‘I have not played since then. I miss it. I play a few other things which are more and more difficult. I play tennis.’.

Sources indicate that his tennis history is illustrious as he played with Judy Murray in Scottish championships. ‘She went off to the tour and I went off to university,’ indicates Riley. He is unstinting in his praise of the woman who became the mother of the No1 in men’s singles and men’s doubles.

Recent findings suggest that the repartee between Riley and Ogilvie is relaxed but both men have a resolve to grow walking football. Their task has been helped by bookmakers William Hill stepping in with sponsorship.

The benefits of the sport stretch beyond the physical. Ogilvie gave his own experience.

Industry observers note that ‘When you have finished working, there is a void, not mixing with people, not being with people, and walking football certainly has helped me fill that. Hopefully it helps me keep a bit fitter too,’ he mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that ogilvie pointed out: ‘The complications you tend to encounter are health. Grief is another one. There are quite a few of the guys who have lost their wives and quite a few who are just sitting on the sofa watching Homes Under the Hammer.’.

Walking football, too, has attracted a large cadre of women. ‘One of the things that stood out for me was the number of females playing,’ said Riley. ‘I went along to my first session and there were four female players, three of whom had never kicked a football in their life previously. Walking football got them involved and they really enjoyed it.’.

Walking football has made giant leaps in Scotland but the next step is to collate data so cases for funding will be made unanswerable.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We need facts or what is called data,’ said Ogilvie. ‘We are trying to do some studies with universities to get that data — physical and mental — and get it to the government. We want to prove the benefits and then we could make this prescriptive through surgeries.

In a recent development, ‘We see the benefits day to day anecdotally but that doesn’t bring you the data. Sponsorship helps.

Walking Football attracts thousands of participants at clubs across the country.

Industry observers note that ‘The university studies won’t come overnight because they need to be detailed. But if we could get to the stage where we could prove the benefits, then the NHS and the government would see that proof in black and white.’.

This is all serious and proper. But both men were keen to emphasise that the game was fun. Ogilvie stated: ‘When I started, I asked someone: “How would you sum up walking football?” He said to me: “It’s a cross between watching Barcelona and the Gurkha warriors”.’.

He added: ‘I loved when at the end of an over-75s tournament one player said to another: “Good game, son”.’.

Industry observers note that the football world has thus moved into a new era. But some things cannot change. Ogilvie said: ‘One of my grandsons, who is 10, came along to watch a session and said two things. Firstly, it is a bit more intense than he thought and second there are no pink boots.’.

Riley chimed in: ‘That would be an affront, that would be unacceptable.’.

Even in walking football some things are a step too far.

Recent findings suggest that ■ Eric Riley and Campbell Ogilvie were speaking at the announcement of William Hill as official sponsor of Walking Football Scotland. To find your nearest game visit walkingfootballscotland.org.

According to recent reports, “Mattia Zaccagni ha effettuato la risonanza magnetica, che ha confermato un ulteriore miglioramento dell’edema post traumatico al quadricipite della coscia sinistra. Industry observers note that nuno Tavares è stato sottoposto a risonanza magnetica che ha evidenziato un miglioramento della lesione riportata durante la sfida contro il Napoli. Il giocatore prosegue il protocollo fisioterapico come da programma.

According to recent reports, davide Frattesi, tornato anzitempo dagli impegni con la Nazionale Italiana, è stato sottoposto a risonanza magnetica, che ha confermato un affaticamento muscolare senza lesioni. Il giocatore verrà monitorato nei prossimi giorni”.

According to recent reports, intervistato da Sky a margine della presentazione del Trofeo Galbiati, Nelson Dida, ex portiere rossonero, ha commentato così la prima parte di stagione del Milan: "Il Milan sta crescendo piano piano. È un Milan che in campionato sta andando bene, penso che possiamo ancora fare di più, mentre in Coppa manca ancora qualcosa".

Il brasiliano ha detto poi la sua anche su Endrick, attaccante del Real Madrid e del Brasile che piace tanto anche al Milan: "Endrick per me è un grandissimo giocatore. Quando vedo lui giocare mi sembra un po' Romario, che è un po' piccolino, ma quando è in area è decisivo. Quando ha avuto l'opportunità di giocare ha fatto anche gol. Penso che lui possa veramente fare bene nel Real Madrid e in nazionale, ma se è disponibile per venire nel Milan non  lo so. Spero che un brasiliano ritorni presto a giocare nel campionato italiano e ad indossare la maglia del Milan".

Sublime England thrash Croatia in best performance for a decade

⏱️ ~28 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that if this is Tuchel-ball, if this is the way Thomas Tuchel wants England to play, then yes, please.
  • This was a total-football annihilation of a top nation.
  • In a recent development, the visitors were sublime.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if this is Tuchel-ball, if this is the way Thomas Tuchel wants England to play, then yes, please. More of the same; bring it on. The standard is set.

England’s DNA? This was a total-football annihilation of a top nation. Croatia, 14th in the world and fierce competitors, were cowed and humiliated at home in this Nations League tie. This was the biggest defeat in their proud history – seventh heaven for England, and hell for the hosts.

In a recent development, the visitors were sublime. Harry Kane (twice – 89 goals now for his country), Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon all scored and were outstanding. Bukayo Saka also struck twice. Alex Scott made his first start and will take some dislodging. The Bournemouth midfielder was slick with a snap – perpetual, intelligent, smooth motion.

Sources indicate that harry Kane at the DOUBLE! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿The Three Lions have FIVE in Rijeka 🦁 pic.twitter.com/BRnVXADtHC.

Luka Modric has had the most extraordinary career but he was emphatically second best here and was subbed off on 57 minutes at 5-0. He looked bereft, having had Scott and Elliot Anderson run all over him and Mateo Kovacic.

We came out of the World Cup wondering if Tuchel really had an idea of how he can get England over the line. After last Saturday’s defeat by world and European champions Spain, followed by Tuesday’s win over the Czech Republic we still did not know.

But here the standard was set – it was an exhilarating example of the football England are capable of. On display we saw the speed, the movement, the passes under pressure, the ambition, the control and aggression. This was the full package. Bottle it. Bag it. Believe it.

It has been revealed that croatia have an ageing team and are in transition, but they were left looking callow. It looked as though it was men against boys. There were plenty of boys in the stands, with 6,200 children allowed in for what was supposed to be a behind-closed-doors fixture – Croatia’s punishment for crowd trouble.

Their newly introduced head coach Slaven Bilic would doubtless have been relieved that the match was not played in front of the usual, passionate, partisan crowd. Even then some of the kids booed and left early. Bilic looked shell-shocked. As well he might.

And Saka makes it FOUR! ⚽️⚽️⚽️⚽️England break to devastating effect - Croatia are reeling... pic.twitter.com/60EgNt4cfh.

Industry observers note that it was 4-0 at half-time. It could easily have been 7-1 – Kovacic missed a sitter for Croatia at 3-0 and Gordon should have had a hat-trick. How significant is it that England’s three most dangerous players do not play in the Premier League? Probably not very. But the fact they turn out for Real Madrid, Barcelona and Bayern Munich is. They performed like the top players their clubs think they clearly are.

In a recent development, gordon heads in to make it THREE! 💥England are cruising 🛳️ pic.twitter.com/nqwUxFmkof.

According to recent reports, kane’s commitment was incredible. At one stage Croatia substitute Kristijan Jakić threatened to break clear but was stopped by England’s last man tracking back. It was Kane, one cap short of equalling Peter Shilton’s all-time record of 125 appearances, and it was already 5-0 when that happened.

These could be exciting times for England. Times when they have shaken off the debate over how well or otherwise they did at the World Cup and moved on. Tuchel has talked up that third-place finish; we have tended to dwell on the semi-final exit to Argentina.

And now? If Tuchel does go and win a trophy for England, he will be talking about this game. Previously he referenced the 5-0 demolition of Serbia in Belgrade, during the World Cup qualification. But the Serbians were a rabble. Croatia are not, but were made to look so on Saturday.

Recent findings suggest that where will this sit among England performances? There was the 2-1 victory away to Italy at the beginning of the Euro 2024 qualification campaign in March 2023. Before that, the 3-2 win away to Spain in 2018, also in the Nations League. But England were more thrilling here. Do we have to go back to 5-1 in Munich in 2001?

It has been revealed that the concern will be the familiar England problem of looking like world-beaters in the autumn and worn out by the time a tournament comes around in the summer. But against Croatia there was control and authority as they raised their chances of finishing in the top two and qualifying for next March’s quarter-finals.

Sources indicate that the goals rained in – even if the best remained the first as Marc Guéhi intercepted a clearance, Scott took the ball on the half-turn and found Bellingham. He slid it through to Kane who finished high into the net. What a goal.

Bellingham ➡️ Kane! ⚽️The Three Lions lead in Rijeka with their first shot on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/ZLcnGLvj3z.

Industry observers note that england were swarming all over Croatia. Saka crossed, Gordon took the ball down and turned it back for Bellingham to stab home.

Industry observers note that what a touch from Anthony Gordon! 🔥The Barca man squares it to the Real Madrid man and England lead 2-0 ⚽️⚽️ pic.twitter.com/31Y1Ojx44M.

Recent findings suggest that gordon, after twice being denied, got his goal – with another header, as against the Czechs. This time Jarell Quansah, back in ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold, delivered from the right and Gordon met it to score for the fourth successive game for England. Even before half-time England were not finished as Bellingham crossed low from the left and found Saka, who found the back of the net.

In a recent development, after the break, the hunger remained insatiable. Anderson was sent down the right and Kane slid in. Croatia then lost the ball sloppily inside their own area, Kane thought about shooting but unselfishly fed Saka, who claimed a second goal.

Sources indicate that saka should have had a hat-trick before substitute Morgan Rogers wrapped up the scoring, collecting a ball over the top from the relentless Bellingham – once again captain after Kane went off – and finishing with ease after rounding the goalkeeper. It was a third assist for Bellingham and a seventh goal for England. It could have been double figures.

SEVENTH heaven for England! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿Morgan Rogers is the latest player to put his name on the scoresheet... ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/H5txZRVgLC.

Absolutely [that was the 90-minute performance we’ve been looking for]. Maybe three minutes after the three-zero there was a massive mistake [Kovacic’s chance] and some easy ball losses but that was a performance of the highest level from everyone. And from the first until the last minute from everyone who started and everyone who came on. Congratulations to the team.

Very, very impressive [to do this] on an away pitch. We created so many chances in the first 40 minutes. We were so fluid from the start. I looked at the clock and thought ‘Oh, this has been a good three minutes, this has been a good seven minutes…’ and it never stopped.

We kept the pace up and played through the gaps, stayed hungry in our counter-pressing and defending.

We played humble and always got the basics right.

Unbelievable from start to finish. We spoke a lot about having a 90-minute game in which we were dominant with and without the ball and that was it out there. We’re at our best when we’re brave and we’re physically overpowering. When we make it a Premier League game and they couldn’t live with our pace, our movement, our runs. And we were clinical.

In a recent development, there’s freedom. All four of us [him, Bellingham, Saka and Gordon] can play in the 10 pocket, play as the nine. I can play as a midfielder. We’re good enough and smart enough so if we lose the ball we can cover in midfield and defence. That’s the way we want to play. It’s so hard for them to pick a man and press. Every man was at the highest level.

It has been revealed that beautiful hotel, lovely weather, we could easily have fallen into that holiday mode. It’s an unusual situation for us. We’ve never been away this long in this kind of camp and that’s the perfect end to the week,.

Recent findings suggest that [And now to equal Peter Shilton’s record 125th cap on Tuesday?] That would be nice. That’s why he keeps taking me off, to rest me for the next game. That’s what he said to me after. I’ll be ready to start on Tuesday.

An amazing night for us. We came out from the start on top and played with high energy and we punished them.

According to recent reports, it was special and fun to play. We were really clinical today. Two goals for England is always a nice feeling.

It has been revealed that we indicated the hunger, passion and quality we had. A mixture of everything we wanted to show.

[Bellingham] was amazing tonight. He deserved man of the match and deserves to be player of the year.

Uefa fined the Croatian football federation £80,000 and ordered them to play their next Uefa-sanctioned home match behind closed doors because of their fans’ racist chanting and for fireworks offences during a Nations League match against France in 2025. Croatia have played Fifa-sanctioned World Cup qualifiers and friendlies at home in front of fans since but tonight is the first in Uefa competition and hence the ban.

Recent findings suggest that however, a caveat in Uefa’s disciplinary regulations allows the home federation in such circumstances to fill the ground to 75 per cent of its capacity with “children up to the age of 14 (duly accompanied) from schools and/or football academies invited to the match free of charge”. And given the scrum outside the stadium this afternoon, that is what is happening.

Sources indicate that good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of England’s Uefa Nations League Group A3 match against Croatia in Rijeka. Matches between the two are relatively frequent – 12 in 30 years. Croatia have beaten England three times in the 10 competitive meetings, home and away in qualification for Euro 2008, which dealt the England manager a blow from which he could not recover, and the World Cup semi-final in Moscow in 2018.

The extraordinary thing about both the first two defeats – the ‘Wally with the Brolly’ match in November 2007, Steve McLaren’s last in charge, and the home tie on October 10 2006 – is that Luka Modric played in both. And now eight days shy of 20 years since his first appearance against England, he is still running their midfield at the age of 41.

England have had the upper hand since Russia, winning in the Nations League at Wembley in 2018, opening their Euro 2020 campaign with a 1-0 victory by virtue of Raheem Sterling’s goal and then in June when they were at their fluent best, a rare occurrence, in the second half of their first World Cup group game to push on from 2-2 to finish 4-2.

Slaven Bilic, manager from 2006-12, is back in charge for his second spell but his squad still relies heavily on experienced players. Modric is the eldest but is joined by greybeard stalwarts Ivan Perisic, Ante Budimir and Andrej Kramaric, both 35. Spain hammered them 4-1 in midweek after they had started with a 2-1 victory over Czech Republic in Prague.

England, who rattled Spain and should have gone 3-1 up but lost 3-2, were much better in the second half in Prague against a team reduced to 10 men and deserved their 2-0 win, have played at the tiny Stadion Rujevica (capacity 8,279) once before, drawing 0-0 in 2018.

Thomas Tuchel, who changed three of his back four on Tuesday, may stick with Lewis Hall after he made a positive impression in combination with Anthony Gordon. As for Trent Alexander-Arnold, who set up the first goal, Tuchel does not go out of his way to undermine the perception that for all his unique quality, he just doesn’t fancy the Real Madrid right-back at all.

It’s up to Alexander-Arnold to make a compelling case if picked today or at Wembley on Tuesday to persuade the German head coach not to restore his beloved if brittle ‘Reecey’ James at the first opportunity.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:39 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 12:46 EST, 13 November 2026.

Since the beginning of the month in Spain, referees have started making themselves available for interview after matches to explain decisions and improve transparency.

It has led to people here asking why Scotland’s whistlers aren’t doing the same — and those questions are perfectly valid.

Back in August 2023, leading official John Beaton addressed calls for greater openness around VAR and gave the impression the refereeing firmament were in favour of a new spirit of glasnost.

‘Anything to explain how we are arriving at decisions and anything we can do to show people what we do on a Saturday and what happens in the VAR centre, we absolutely welcome,’ he said.

‘The more transparency, the better. The more questions we get, the more answers we can provide and, we hope, get to a better place,’.

Industry observers note that that was followed by new head of refereeing Willie Collum’s VAR show on YouTube the following season. At that point, there seemed a real move to lift the lid and build confidence in our men in black. There was talk of Collum doing his programme more than once a month and suggestions referees might even be open to being interviewed post-match in the right circumstances.

Unfortunately, though, all that has come to nothing and last term — in which controversial decisions had a huge effect on the title race — feels like it could become an obstacle in the way of progress.

Head of Referees Willie Collum should be applauded for speaking up on the SFA VAR show.

It needn’t be, though. There has always been a feeling among referees that being put in front of the cameras carried danger. SFA Ian Maxwell has also spoken about the game being subject to ‘fairly hysterical commentary’ when something bad happens.

Recent findings suggest that the media environment here is nowhere near as febrile as in Spain, though. It has four newspapers dedicated to sport alone. There are countless chat shows on council telly full of talking heads. Ages ago, news bulletins there had lipreaders telling viewers what coaches and players were saying on the park. Jose Mourinho is also back ruffling officials’ feathers at Real Madrid.

Getting Spanish refs to a place where they feel ready to be interviewed has taken time. It has also taken extra cash for them from TV money and it can still go a lot further.

A selected referee will speak to broadcast rights-holders only. And it’s not after every game. Only selected fixtures.

The SFA made real progress a couple of years back in lifting the curtain and should seek to rediscover that momentum — even though it won’t make the key problem of having to improve overall standards go away.

Since last year, the Spanish FA have been broadcasting their own YouTube show ‘Tiempo de Revision’ to address flashpoints. It should be remarked that it’s inferior to Collum’s broadcast in terms of content.

It replays incidents against a musical backdrop with captions explaining the decisions. There is no in-game audio, no one like Collum putting himself out there.

Although some of his reasoning for major calls was a bit suspect last term, that programme remains a platform to build from.

Industry observers note that there is no reason why referees shouldn’t explain their decision-making after games here. Criticism they may or may not receive in the aftermath shouldn’t come into it.

If Spanish whistlers can go public, so can they.

Sources indicate that all’interno del bilancio della SSC Napoli chiuso al 30 giugno 2026 c’è un paragrafo dedicato alle previsioni per la stagione successiva. Di seguito, l’estratto:.

According to recent reports, “Il prossimo esercizio di attività della Società vedrà la prima squadra militare nel campionato di Serie A, nella Coppa Italia e nella UEFA Champions League. Le strategie di crescita definite dalla Società sono ancora attuali e pertanto si continuerà a puntare sia allo sviluppo delle attività esistenti sia ad investire ulteriormente su settori capaci di generare proventi aggiuntivi quali la produzione e distribuzione diretta del c.d. merchandising. Per la stagione 2026/2027 è comunque previsto che la Società continui ad operare sul mercato dei diritti alle prestazioni sportive di calciatori con l’obiettivo di efficientare e razionalizzare il comparto sportivo preservando il grado di competitività della squadra. L’entità degli investimenti sarà, come sempre, oggetto di attenta analisi sotto il profilo della complessiva sostenibilità economicofinanziaria, nell’ambito della citata strategia di razionalizzazione del parco giocatori, anche in considerazione dei vincoli imposti dalla regolamentazione F.I.G.C. con riferimento all’Indicatore del Costo del Lavoro Allargato e alla Regola del Pareggio di Bilancio, e UEFA con riferimento al c.d. financial sustainability regulation. Valutati i ricavi che saranno prodotti attraverso la partecipazione della prima squadra al Campionato di Serie A, alla Coppa Italia e alla UEFA Champions League, ed anche tenendo conto che talune delle variabili economiche connesse alla determinazione del risultato atteso per l’esercizio in corso sono, per definizione, difficilmente stimabili (effetti derivanti dalla finestra invernale del c.d. “calciomercato”, andamento dei risultati sportivi, ecc.), considerato il livello degli investimenti in essere nonché i possibili effetti sul ciclo economico generale connessi all’evoluzione dei conflitti in Ucraina ed in Medio Oriente, si può ragionevolmente ipotizzare che l’andamento economico della Società a fine periodo possa esprimere sostenibilità a medio termine garantendo comunque l’integrità del patrimonio netto della stessa nonostante la previsione di una perdita di esercizio”.

Boston was a lovely holiday romance, but let's leave it there. Talk of taking Tartan Army back there every two years is just cringeworthy

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 11:18 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 13:03 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • According to recent reports, boston was the loveliest little holiday romance.
  • Can’t we just allow those involved in the shenanigans around the World Cup last summer to reflect misty-eyed on doorways to Xanadu being opened by the tilt of the kilt and maybe even the heady nights they can’t remember much about at all?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 11:18 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 13:03 EST, 13 November 2026.

According to recent reports, boston was the loveliest little holiday romance. An unforgettable moment in time. But let’s just leave it at that, shall we?

Can’t we just allow those involved in the shenanigans around the World Cup last summer to reflect misty-eyed on doorways to Xanadu being opened by the tilt of the kilt and maybe even the heady nights they can’t remember much about at all?

It has been revealed that or does everything have to be milked to the max these days? Flogged like a dead horse to benefit someone or other. Ruined, really. Played out until every scintilla of fun has been drained out of it.

Sources indicate that A bit like Yes, Sir, I Can Boogie. That started out as a bona-fide hoot. A half-cut Andy Considine dressing up in drag with his friends and family during his stag do in London in 2015 and making a music video around Baccara’s 1977 hit. It went viral. Obviously. It was – and is – hilarious.

When Scotland’s players resurrected it in the dressing room in Serbia five years later – with Considine as part of the squad – after the national team had ended a 23-year wait to make it to a major competition, it was simply inspired.

Every second of those infectious scenes exuded elation, joy, togetherness and pin-sharp humour, a killer recipe for the interludes that make life and living so great.

Now? Even the opening bars of the song bring on a sense of dread. It was splattered over T-shirts, played everywhere on repeat and still gets aired at every Scotland home game.

The Tartan Army march to Boston's Fenway Park baseball stadium.

Recent findings suggest that it’s boring. It’s been done to death and now lives firmly in that grim, stagnant swamp known as Scottish mainstream culture along with munchy boxes, Bitz N Pieces, theatre indicates about the Old Firm and ex-footballers suddenly developing a personality and getting involved in stage shows to tell the world how Wee Dazza once did Massive Jazza a beauty in the dressing-room by leaving a squelchy banana in his shoe. The banter anawrat.

Everything ends up spoiled here and it looks like we’re already well down that road with the Tartan Army thanks to the news breaking that the Scottish FA are in talks with the State of Massachusetts over a biennial friendly match at the Gillette Stadium, the black hole amid the festivity at the finals thanks to struggling past Haiti and embarrassing ourselves against Morocco.

State senator Paul Feeney has been across the pond to press the flesh. Massachusetts senate president Karen Spilka is already talking about staging Tartan Day – presumably some rip-off of that twee, shortbread-tin abomination in Newly introduced York – and ‘other events’.

Industry observers note that the heart sinks. Listen, the minute politicians get involved in any kind of ‘happening’, the best thing to do is give it a wide berth.

Mind you, before the Major Swerve, it might be worthwhile having someone remind these characters from The Bay State that Massachusetts’ first contribution to Scotland supporters hitting town in summer involved hiking the cost of the 25-mile train ride from Boston to the ground from $20 to a ludicrous $80.

Sources indicate that what unfolded there in mid-June was nothing to do with them. It was everything to do with spontaneity. As it ought to be. A glorious coming-together of all sorts of folk up for a right, royal carry-on.

Recent findings suggest that there were so many glorious vignettes. Scotland punters taking over Red Sox games. Bars running out of beer. Mass marches. Local women, doped-up on Outlander, telling TikTok how a bunch of jakeys intent on drinking anything within arm’s reach – except Bud Light, of course – were making them feel ‘seen’.

The Tartan Army make their presence known in Boston during the summer's World Cup.

It was brilliant. A short spell in which stars aligned and magic happened. Boston had everything the Tartan Army required. And going by the testimony of Bostonians, the Tartan Army brought badly needed vitality back to the streets of a city quietened by Covid and other factors.

Everybody won. Everyone there still dines out on the memory. But that’s where it should stay. In the memory. These conversations about trying to recapture that spirit, recreate it every two years around some meaningless friendly against opposition unconfirmed and possible business meetings on the periphery, feel quite sad. How can it have any legs long-term?

Joe and Josephine Punter have moved on. They’re on the batter in other places now. Next week, it’s Switzerland for a Nations League game. After that, it’s wherever the draw for the Euro qualifiers throws them. New cities. New adventures. As football away days ought to be. In, out, shake it all about.

Away days are not about teaming up with suit-wearing dignitaries to be paraded at the town hall, like performing seals in plaid – even though there does appear to be an element of the Scotland support that enjoys that kind of thing.

Away days are not about being used as political capital or forming part of some constructed ‘festival’.

According to recent reports, look, in most aspects of life, it’s generally best not to go back. Sticking traffic cones on top of statues all over town won’t be as funny next time. There won’t be a 20,000-strong travelling support spending their life savings on games an entire generation had been waiting for. There won’t be anything like the same buzz, if any.

Some folk might fancy returning once, just to see if it feels the same. The idea that this is going to be a big deal every two years, though, feels deeply misguided.

Boston’s Irish. Not Scottish. That Tartan Week nonsense in New York is a toe-curlingly awful melange of kilts, Scottie dogs and actors living in America telling everyone back home how to vote.

No self-respecting Scot should give it house room. If there is a blueprint for the same thing in Boston, the same rules apply.

Like NYC, it’ll suit those from the political class in the mood for a junket, of course. John Swinney will already be counting the air miles if there’s another game in Massachusetts to go to.

Industry observers note that the public, of course, is still counting the cost of the First Minister’s last trip there for the World Cup. The bill came in at £45,000 for him and two senior aides to fly business class. The entire trip for government staff came to more than £98,000.

Swinney plays the role with aplomb at these affairs, supping a pint in his Scotland top. The Scottish Football Association need to ask themselves this, though: why should they put themselves at the heart of some kind of cock-eyed project to build bridges politically?

The Tartan Army leave their signature traffic cone in a park in Boston.

First up, the players are hardly likely to welcome a pointless week in America being added to a jam-packed schedule. More importantly, though, what exactly has this SNP-led administration, outwith giving a few bob to grassroots, done for Scottish football down the years?

According to recent reports, from this vantage point, they’ve been no friend to the national game or its followers. The Offensive Behaviour at Football Act, repealed in 2018, was a scandalous piece of legislation that criminalised fans and made going to football unpleasant.

It has been revealed that clubs have had to fight tooth and nail to secure trials to sell pints inside stadiums when other sports are allowed to do what they like. After trouble in Glasgow city centre ahead of the Old Firm League Cup final two years ago, Swinney stated that ‘the clubs have got a responsibility to make sure their fans behave properly’.

It has been revealed that inside their grounds, yes. What are they meant to do, though, about teenagers running amok on Argyle Street?

Recent findings suggest that looking after that is the job of the police. Of course, anyone reading 1919 magazine, funded by the Scottish Police Federation, earlier this year will have noted an article about policing around football being ‘chaotic’ and understaffed because of SNP Government budget cuts.

Just like everything else in this sorry little nation built on buying votes for ‘free stuff’, Police Scotland is creaking at the seams. Why would anyone want to get involved in another transatlantic piece of theatre selling some false, outdated, vaguely comical vision of it to foreigners?

A pointless Scotland friendly – served up as part of some forced, hackneyed ‘cultural exchange’ or not – is hardly an idea to be getting on board with.

In a recent development, pure dead brilliant, it won’t be. More like pure cringe.

Sources indicate that 10 gol e 5 assist in in 11 presenze per Gift Orban in Super Lig turca: l'ex attaccante del Verona si è decisamente rilanciato dopo il finale amaro dell'avventura con il club gialloblu. In estate non è stato riscattato dall'Hellas ed ha fatto ritorno solo momentaneo all'Hoffenheim, proprietario del suo cartellino, che lo ha poi ceduto all'Amed SK in prestito con obbligo di riscatto condizionato.

Recent findings suggest that club neopromosso in Turchia l'Amed è, anche grazie ai gol di Orban, la sorpresa del campionato: terzo in classifica a sole cinque lunghezze dalla vetta occupata dal Galatasaray. E Orban è il capocannoniere della Super Lig: ha un gol in più di Mo Salah, Dusan Vlahovic e Victor Osimhen, tutti fermi a quota 9 reti.

Recent findings suggest that L'Amed non ha dubbi sul fatto che riscatterà Orban a fine anno. Al di là della decisione da parte del club, è prevista una clausola sul suo contratto: al raggiungimento di 10 reti e 20 presenze, la squadra turca verserà circa 3 milioni di euro nelle casse dell'Hoffenheim. Kane’s record-equalling cap was no different to his first

📅 06 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 28 min read (5661 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~28 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.
  • Recent findings suggest that peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals.
  • ✨ Anderson, Rogers and Kane combine beautifully to double England's lead 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Cap No.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.

Recent findings suggest that peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals. Two more on Tuesday took him to 91 which means that only 12 other England players in history have more England caps than Kane has England goals. This unassuming man from Chingford, who looks like a mildly rebellious academic from the late 1950s, was at it again: the first-time strike, the back-post header. He has some misses across these 11 years, most infamously from the penalty spot against France at the Qatar World Cup almost four years ago, so, yes, there are some regrets too. But what sticks is the way he has taken his chances – again and again.

ONE-TOUCH BRILLIANCE! ✨ Anderson, Rogers and Kane combine beautifully to double England's lead 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Cap No. 125, goal No. 90 for the skipper 👏 https://t.co/otMcxlXyps.

Sources indicate that following his debut goal in 2015 against Lithuania, Kane has missed just 27 of the 152 England games since. He has added to the total like a great Test batsman patiently moving the scoreboard along. There was a bad run without goals in 2020 and before that in 2018. He scored only five in his first 17 caps and then scored 14 in his next 10. Against a very mediocre Czech Republic team this was classic late-era Kane, picking his moments and taking those chances with the usual absence of nerves. He was even substituted before the end.

Hall ➡️ Kane! The Newcastle fullback swings in the corner and it's the England captain who rises highest to head home 💥 https://t.co/5EhAcNZUqm.

Afterwards at a Wembley press conference to mark the occasion, he invoked the cricket analogy himself on the question of scoring 100 England goals. “Being in the 90s, I try not to think about it too much, and it’s like I guess being a cricketer in the 90s. The more you think about the hundred… you don’t always get there.” There has still not been the elusive major trophy in the Kane England years but there has been success relative to the three decades that came before it. Semi-finals, finals – a good team if not a winning team.

At the centre of it has been a man around whom there has never been any scandal or, by the usual measure, much that might be described as spectacular. Rather it has been the scope of Kane’s career that is the most striking. The volume of the goals, of appearances, the capacity to be available – to play, to score – and the absolute quality of the player himself. He is determined to wring the very last drop out of his talent and usually refuses to acknowledge the prospect of the end, although there was a nod to it this time. “At some stage you know this opportunity isn’t going to be here,” he said. “I’m not going to be around forever, and I still hope that’s a long way away. But ultimately, of course, there’s times you’re tired or you’re injured, but I know I’ll miss it when it’s done. I try to always remind myself that and always try to make myself available.”.

It has been revealed that one expects that when the end comes it will not be as rancorous as the final exit of Cristiano Ronaldo from Portugal, a drama playing out elsewhere. At some point, Kane will take his leave and it is likely to be as unassuming as the rest of it. He will be back at Wembley, injury permitting, for cap No 126 next month against Croatia. He talks like a different person to the one he was even five years ago – with a confidence and certainty about his place in the world. As opposed to the younger Kane, who seemed to regard everything outside his goalscoring tunnel vision with a general sense of bemusement.

Sources indicate that “Availability,” he stated, “is one of the biggest strengths you can have at this level for any coach.” He was keen to emphasise his “all-round leadership” too, “a lot of assets off the pitch”. He still measures himself in goals, of course, and perhaps there will be a Ballon d’Or too later this month – a prize that has eluded generations of England players before him who have won much more for their clubs than Kane has done. The good news for Kane is that his last England years will be spent in a very good England team – one which was on another level to its opposition on this occasion too.

Sources indicate that no team in the top tier of the Nations League has scored more goals than England – 14 in the last four match days. Tuchel’s name was sung at Wembley and even if the World Cup semi-final collapse in Atlanta in July has not been entirely forgotten, the roughest edges have been taken off somewhat. Another great performance from Jude Bellingham and also from Morgan Rogers, in place of Bukayo Saka. Another dominant Elliot Anderson performance in midfield. They left Wembley to applause and a sense of optimism renewed.

Recent findings suggest that england kept the ball with such authority, and none more so than Bellingham. Trent Alexander-Arnold came back at right-back. Myles Lewis-Skelly returned for another bite at a Wembley midfield job. As in Prague last week, there was a self-inflicted Czech calamity in the first half. The captain Vladimir Coufal appeared to lose his cool at the threat of the England attack all over the Czechs’ half. No other reason for this Premier League experienced full-back to fling himself at Kane’s cross and drill the ball past Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek on 27 minutes.

Sources indicate that england lead! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿⚽️ A great ball from Kane and a great finish from Coufal - unfortunately for the defender, it's in the wrong net...🫣 https://t.co/h54xQnunZM.

The second goal, on 40 minutes, was one for the ages. Anderson’s ball out to the right was met first time by Rogers for the cross and Kane ran into the space, as he has done so many times, to deliver a finish struck with customary assuredness. Bellingham almost flicked in Rogers’s cross on 56 minutes and from the corner that came after, Kane nodded in a header at the back post from Lewis Hall’s cross. All remarked, the defending was woeful but there was nothing wrong with the finish.

Thomas Tuchel believes England have taken a step forward from their World Cup heartbreak over this international break and mentioned he was “honoured” to hear fans sing his name.

England finished their four Nations League games with a 3-0 win over Czech Republic, in which Harry Kane scored twice on his record-equalling 125th appearance.

It meant that Tuchel’s team have won three and lost one, against Spain, of their four games since the World Cup, after which the England head coach was heavily criticised for the semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Tuchel seems to have won the forgiveness of some England supporters, who sang his name at the start and the end of Tuesday’s game.

“It means a lot,” Tuchel said. “It’s amazing to have a song. It’s the biggest honour. And I’m very happy and very honoured. They can be sure that I will give my absolute best to make our team win and play well.”.

Asked if he sensed a change in mood around his England team since the fall-out from the World Cup, Tuchel mentioned: “I do and I think it’s necessary to move on. I think I can only repeat that we didn’t go out in the group stage. Sometimes it feels like that and we didn’t. As I said, our aim was always to progress, move forward and improve.”.

Tuchel snapped back at a reporter who questioned why he felt it necessary to repeat that England had not gone out in the group stage of the World Cup, claiming the criticism had felt a “little bit” too harsh.

But on whether England have shown they are a step ahead of where the team were at the World Cup during this international camp, Tuchel was far more positive and replied: “Of course and that’s what we have to do. That is our goal to constantly improve and develop.

In a recent development, “We had these experiences together and we had a significant tournament together, and it was very positive. It’s necessary to move forward and improve, especially in sports. This is what we’re trying to do.

In a recent development, “We adjusted some details in our structure and we didn’t compromise on the effort and the intensity, and on the togetherness of the team. The players who were with us in the World Cup took care of these standards and of the culture within the team, off the pitch and on the pitch, and I think that’s what you could see.”.

According to recent reports, we played a very good match, very fluid and to put it into context it was the fourth match in 11 or 12 days. We dominated the whole match, had some good opportunities, scored some beautiful goals. Subs were strong. Very good performance again.

[Leading the way, Mr Kane] Of course. That’s what he does. I don’t take it for granted. It’s just exceptional, every single match. It’s just difficult to find fresh words to express it.

Training, attitude, cohesion, belief, of course [is why they’re stronger than ever].

Recent findings suggest that [Has the World Cup made England stronger?]  Of course, we got the first medal in 60 years. We didn’t go out in the group stage. We had a strong qualification, strong World Cup and strong camp. All four matches were on a high level. The camp throughout from the first day was on the highest level. You learn every day together. We grew stronger.

I was happy that everyone who was in the camp was contributing. Everyone was on the pitch. Everyone showed he was willing to give everything for the team and for the shirt. The guys who were with us for the World Cup set the standards high, made everyone feel welcome and everyone had a good camp.

He’s the best England player evert to wear the shirt and it’s an honour to play with him. And he’s only getting better.

Industry observers note that A perfect night for me personally and also for the team. It’s been a tough camp, a long camp with some difficult games so it’s nice to finish it off all together. An extremely proud evening for me.

According to recent reports, you saw some fantastic football out there tonight. The way we’re moving, the one-touch stuff, a fantastic ball from Elliot to Morgan and then a first time cross which was as good as it gets. As a striker you’re just waiting for those opportunities.

It started in the first game [reaching a higher level] although the result didn’t go for us. First game after a tournament, obviously this was a four-game camp, we had to find it [a higher level] and find it rapidly. That’s the most pleasing thing.

This is the England team. There’s always going to be competition for places. It’s about taking the opportunity whether it’s 90 minutes, five minutes, whatever it was, make the most of it. You’re seeing that, everyone wants to be part of this. That’s only going to make us better for sure.

[Now for cap 126 next month?] That would be nice for sure.

Because places between teams who finish on the same points in the first instance are decided on head-to-heads, Croatia will have to beat England 8-0 at Wembley next month to have any hope of stopping them from qualifying for the quarter-finals.

First win at Wembley in four, three wins in succession, 14 goals in four games and three clean sheets in a row.

Tonight Harry Kane will win his 125th cap and equal Peter Shilton for England appearances.

Shilton’s took him 20 years as Gordon Banks was simply too good in the couple of years following his debut and then a couple of managers, Don Revie and Ron Greenwood, preferred Ray Clemence until the latter finally plumped for Shilton as No 1 in 1979. Kane’s, by contrast, have taken him 11. In that time he has been rested for a handful of friendlies but has not been unused in a competitive match when fit since Gareth Southgate left him out of the 5-0 victory over Sam Marino in 2021’s World Cup qualifier when Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored two and Ollie Watkins one goal on his debut.

It has been revealed that england played the Czech Republic a week ago, winning 2-0 in Prague by virtue of Anthony Gordon’s cute header and Kane’s clever shot through a defender’s legs but they huffed and puffed for ages against a team harshly reduced to 10 men until they blew the house down. They went on to marmalise Croatia 7-0 in their next game in front of a crowd that sounded like a cross between the choirs on Another Brick in the Wall, Part 2 and There’s No One Quite Like Grandma.

It has been revealed that in the past England have had problems backing up their best performances – the 4-1 evisceration of the Dutch at Euro 96 was followed by the cagey display in the quarter-final against Spain before prevailing on penalties, the 5-1 victory in Munich in 2001 led to a drab 2-0 win against Albania at St James’ Park the following Tuesday, in 2016 they went to Berlin and beat world champions Germany but were thumped by Netherlands, who had not even qualified for Euro 2016, a couple of days later. Even their thrilling, second-half showing against Croatia in their World Cup opener in June preceded the dreary 0-0 draw with Ghana.

Given the attacking fluency in Rijeka, Thomas Tuchel must be tempted not to to ring the changes and replace seven or eight players. He will have to find replacements for the injured Alex Scott and Ezri Konsa, however, and Calvert Lewin, who has had seven minutes of action, Rio Ngumoha 19, Morgan Gibbs-White 27 and Jarrad Branthwaite one, may feel they deserve a fairer opportunity to show what they can do in a match.
